brief_summary: Sepsis is a major and life-threatening complication in patients with severe burn injuries, frequently progressing to sepsis-induced coagulopathy (SIC) and disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC). Early detection of coagulopathy in burn patients remains challenging due to the massive background inflammatory response triggered by the thermal injury itself. The primary objective of this prospective observational study is to evaluate the diagnostic performance and early kinetic trajectory (from Day 0 to Day 10) of the revised Japanese Association for Acute Medicine (JAAM-2) score for detecting sepsis-induced coagulopathy in severe burn patients. Adult patients with severe thermal burns (\>20% total body surface area) who develop a first episode of sepsis in the intensive care unit (ICU) will be monitored over a 28-day period. Sequential clinical evaluations and laboratory tests will be performed at Day 0 (T0), H48 (Day 2), Day 4, Day 6, Day 8, and Day 10. The study will compare the JAAM-2 score with established coagulopathy scores (ISTH Overt DIC and ISTH-SIC) and analyze its association with organ dysfunction, sepsis control at Day 7, and 28-day overall mortality.
interventions: Prospective calculation and kinetic monitoring of the revised Japanese Association for Acute Medicine (JAAM-2) score using biological parameters (platelet count/kinetics, PT/INR, D-dimer/FDP) measured
lead_sponsor: Center for Traumatology and Major Burns, Ben Arous
primary_outcomes: Diagnostic Accuracy and Early Kinetic Trajectory of the JAAM-2 Score
title: Early Detection and Kinetics of Sepsis-Induced Coagulopathy in Severe Burn Patients

brief_summary:
Brief Summary:

The vast majority of people with HIV (PWH) who adhere to antiretroviral therapy achieve sustained suppression of viral replication. Despite undetectable plasma HIV RNA, HIV DNA persists in latently infected cells, and individuals may differ in their vulnerability to future treatment failure.

Total and intact HIV DNA levels in virologically suppressed PWH have recently attracted interest as potential markers of HIV reservoir size and composition, which may influence the risk of viral rebound, particularly following treatment simplification to regimens with potentially lower antiviral potency.

To investigate the value of HIV DNA as a marker of future treatment vulnerability, this case-control study will collect blood samples retrospectively and prospectively from PWH who experience viral rebound after at least six months of sustained virological suppression (cases) and matched PWH who remain virologically suppressed over the corresponding period (controls). Matching will be based on age, sex, and duration of virological suppression. For each participant, one peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) sample and one plasma sample will be collected within a predefined window, starting at least six months after virological suppression is achieved and ending at least three months before viral rebound in cases or the corresponding reference time in controls. PBMCs will be used to quantify total and intact HIV DNA, while plasma will be analyzed for standard soluble inflammation markers. The study aims to determine whether higher total and/or intact HIV DNA levels predict subsequent virological failure and whether these measures are associated with systemic inflammation markers.

Study Title:

HIV-DNA and Risk of HIV-RNA Rebound After Sustained Suppression (VIROMARKERS WP3-HIV)

Background \& Rationale:

Although antiretroviral therapy (ART) achieves HIV-RNA viral load suppression below 50 copies/mL in over 95% of people living with HIV (PWH), the virus persists in reservoirs and cannot be fully eradicated. Total HIV-DNA is a well-established surrogate marker of the viral reservoir; however, it often overestimates the replication-competent reservoir. The Intact Proviral DNA Assay (IPDA) allows for the specific quantification of intact proviruses capable of replication. While total HIV-DNA and intact proviral DNA show promise as candidate biomarkers to predict the risk and timing of viral rebound, their clinical utility and predictive accuracy in routine patient profiling require consolidated clinical validation. Furthermore, persistent viral expression from the reservoir may trigger chronic immune activation and systemic inflammation despite sustained plasma viral suppression. Study Objectives:To establish a standardized platform across participating research sites for quantifying total and intact HIV-DNA using stored blood, peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC), or purified CD4+ T-cell samples. To evaluate the association between total/intact HIV-DNA levels and the risk of HIV-RNA viral rebound in PWH under sustained virological suppression. To assess the correlation between total/intact HIV-DNA levels and key systemic inflammatory biomarkers during suppressive ART.

Study Design \& Methodology:

This is an international, retrospective, and prospective observational case-control study conducted across well-characterized European cohorts of PWH. The study will analyze a minimum of 300 participants, comprising 100 "cases" who experienced virological rebound and 200 matched "controls" who maintained full virological suppression.

Cases: PWH under suppressive therapy who experienced virological rebound (defined as two consecutive viral loads \>200 copies/mL or a single viral load \>1,000 copies/mL followed by an ART change).

Controls: PWH matched 2:1 to cases based on age, sex, cohort, and duration of HIV-RNA suppression, who maintained HIV-RNA ≤50 copies/mL over the same follow-up timeframe.

Key Eligibility Criteria. Inclusion Criteria: Adults (≥18 years) with confirmed HIV diagnosis enrolled in a cohort with regular viral load monitoring (≥2 values/year); sustained HIV-RNA ≤50 copies/mL for \>6 months under modern ART (started after 2012); availability of stored PBMC, whole blood, and plasma samples collected while suppressed; and at least 2 additional viral load measurements post-baseline.

Exclusion Criteria: Active Hepatitis B Virus (HBV) or Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) coinfection.

Study Procedures \& Biomarker Testing:

Genomic Testing: stored PBMC or whole blood samples collected during viral suppression (at least 3 months prior to rebound for cases) will be analyzed central-site for total HIV-DNA and intact proviral DNA (IPDA).

Proteomic Testing: plasma samples collected at matching timepoints will undergo proteomic evaluation to measure markers of inflammation/immune activation.
primary_outcomes: Association between total and intact human immunodeficiency virus deoxyribonucleic acid (HIV-DNA) levels and the risk of virological rebound
title: HIV-DNA and Risk of HIV-RNA Rebound After Sustained Suppression

brief_summary:
Muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) is a potentially lethal disease for which radical cystectomy with appropriate systemic therapy remains a standard curative approach in medically fit patients. . However, Half of bladder cancer cases are diagnosed in patients aged over 75 years, many of whom are not fit for major surgery owing to their performance status and comorbidities .

A substantial proportion of bladder cancer cases occur in older adults (there is no single universal age cutoff for the term older adults, but several commonly used definitions exist: WHO: generally refers to people aged 60 years or older, particularly in low- and middle-income countries, while in clinical and research settings: ≥65 years is frequently used as the operational definition of older adults, especially in oncology and geriatric medicine), and advanced age is frequently accompanied by comorbidities and frailty that may limit eligibility for radical surgery or multimodality treatment . Bladder-preserving treatment incorporating maximal transurethral resection of bladder tumor (TURBT) and definitive radiotherapy is therefore an important treatment option in selected patients.
primary_outcomes: Assessment of objective Response rate (ORR) and Disease control rate (DCR)
title: Sequential Chemotherapy Followed by Ultrahypofractionated Radiotherapy for Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer

brief_summary: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is frequently accompanied by deficits in executive functions and fine motor skills, which affect daily activities, academic performance, and health-related quality of life. The DextEgg is a gamified hand-training device with motion and pressure sensors that connects to a tablet app and allows fine motor exercises to be combined with cognitive demands (inhibition, working memory, cognitive flexibility). This single-center randomized controlled trial evaluates whether a 4-week home-based cognitive-motor training with the DextEgg improves fine motor skills and executive functions in children aged 8 to 12 years with ADHD, compared with a motor-only DextEgg training of identical dose. Fifty children will be randomized 1:1 and complete 20 home-based sessions (5 per week, 35 minutes each). Assessments take place at baseline, after the intervention, and at 3-month follow-up.
primary_outcomes: Fine motor skills (M-ABC-3 fine motor coordination)
title: Cognitive-Motor Training With the DextEgg in Children With ADHD

brief_summary:
This study will compare inspiratory muscle training and diaphragmatic breathing exercises in individuals with generalized anxiety disorder (GAD). It aims to investigate whether adding either breathing-based intervention to a combined exercise program improves anxiety symptoms and other health-related outcomes compared with adding progressive muscle relaxation.

Participants will be randomly assigned to one of three groups. All groups will receive the same combined exercise program. In addition, the first group will perform inspiratory muscle training, which involves breathing against resistance to strengthen the inspiratory muscles. The second group will perform diaphragmatic breathing exercises, which focus on using the diaphragm during breathing. The third group will receive Jacobson's progressive muscle relaxation technique, which involves systematically tensing and relaxing different muscle groups. All interventions will be delivered over eight weeks using a hybrid telerehabilitation approach combining face-to-face, synchronous online, and independent home-based sessions.

The study will evaluate anxiety symptoms, respiratory muscle strength, pulmonary function, functional exercise capacity, dyspnea, quality of life, depression symptoms, and heart rate variability. The findings may provide further evidence on the comparative effects of these interventions when added to a combined exercise program in individuals with GAD.
primary_outcomes: Change in Anxiety Severity Measured by the GAD-7
title: Inspiratory Muscle Training and Diaphragmatic Breathing in GAD

brief_summary: This study aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of oral ivermectin in adults with recalcitrant genital warts that have not responded to conventional treatments. A total of 90 participants will receive oral ivermectin (200 µg/kg) once weekly for four weeks. Treatment response will be assessed by changes in wart number and size at weeks 2, 4, and 8. Potential adverse effects, recurrence, and patient satisfaction will also be evaluated. The study will help assess the potential role of oral ivermectin in treating persistent or recurrent genital warts.
title: Efficacy and Safety of Oral Ivermectin for Genital Warts

brief_summary: This cross-sectional, observational study evaluates drug utilization patterns and prescribing practices in the ear, nose, and throat (ENT) outpatient department using World Health Organization (WHO) core prescribing indicators. The study aims to assess prescription quality, the average number of drugs per encounter, antibiotic overuse, generic prescribing rates, and adherence to essential medicines lists to promote rational drug use and identify potential polypharmacy trends.
primary_outcomes: Average Number of Drugs Per Prescription
title: Drug Utilization and Prescribing Practices in the ENT Outpatient Department

brief_summary: This prospective, assessor-blinded, controlled observational study compares bleeding after simple tooth extraction between adults aged 40 years or older who continue their antiplatelet therapy (aspirin, clopidogrel or dual antiplatelet therapy) without interruption and controls taking no drug that affects haemostasis. Socket bleeding is graded at 15, 30, 45 and 60 minutes within a stepwise local haemostatic protocol, and recurrent bleeding is monitored by telephone for 72 hours. The study also explores demographic, clinical and pharmacological factors associated with prolonged and recurrent bleeding among patients on antiplatelet therapy.
interventions: Simple tooth extraction with stepwise local haemostatic protocol
lead_sponsor: University of Medicine and Pharmacy at Ho Chi Minh City
primary_outcomes: Proportion of Sockets With Residual Bleeding at 15 Minutes
Proportion of Sockets With Residual Bleeding at 30 Minutes
title: Post-extraction Bleeding in Older Adults on Uninterrupted Antiplatelet Therapy

brief_summary:
To evaluate the pharmacokinetic characteristics of a single intravenous injection of KL0011034 injection in healthy non-elderly and elderly trial participants.

To evaluate the pharmacodynamics and safety of a single intravenous injection of KL0011034 injection in healthy non-elderly and elderly trial participants.
title: A Study to Evaluate the PK/PD and Safety of KL0011034 Injection in Healthy Non-Elderly and Elderly Trial Participants

brief_summary: This study aims to investigate the effectiveness of high-intensity electromagnetic stimulation using the BTL-6000 Super Inductive System (SIS) in the management of hemiplegic shoulder pain in patients with stroke. Hemiplegic shoulder pain is a common complication following stroke and may negatively affect upper limb function, participation in rehabilitation, and quality of life. The study will evaluate whether treatment with the Super Inductive System can reduce shoulder pain and improve shoulder-related clinical outcomes. The findings are expected to contribute to the evidence regarding non-invasive physical therapy approaches for hemiplegic shoulder pain.
lead_sponsor: Gaziler Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation Education and Research Hospital
primary_outcomes: Visual Analog Scale (VAS) for Shoulder Pain
title: Effectiveness of High-intensity Peripheral Magnetic Stimulation on Hemiplegic Shoulder Pain After Stroke

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate efficacy and safety of once-weekly SHR-3167 and once-daily Insulin Degludec in participants with Type 2 diabetes that has been treated with basal insulin. The study consists of a screening period, a treatment period and a safety follow-up period. The study will last up to 33 weeks.
title: A Study Comparing SHR-3167 With Insulin Degludec in Adults With Type 2 Diabetes Currently Treated With Basal Insulin

brief_summary: This randomized controlled trial evaluated whether an 8-week expressive arts therapy (EAT) program can improve emotion regulation and reduce aggression in male violent offenders incarcerated in a Chinese prison. A total of 65 participants were randomly assigned to an EAT intervention group (n=31) or a routine-care control group (n=34). The program used art, clay, and music to help participants express emotions and reinterpret negative experiences.
conditions: Emotion Dysregulation and Aggressive Behavior in Violent Offenders
title: Art Therapy For Violent Offenders

brief_summary:
Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) is a common and potentially persistent side effect of neurotoxic chemotherapy, characterized by symptoms such as numbness, tingling, pain, and sensory dysfunction in the hands and feet. These symptoms may negatively affect physical functioning, quality of life, and participation in daily activities.

Exercise therapy has emerged as a promising non-pharmacological intervention for individuals with CIPN. However, it remains unclear which exercise approach is most effective. Neurodynamic interventions have shown beneficial effects in other peripheral neuropathic conditions but have not yet been adequately investigated in individuals with CIPN.

The objective of the CIPN-NEXT trial is to evaluate the effectiveness of two exercise-based rehabilitation programmes in individuals with CIPN. Participants will be randomized to one of three study arms: (1) aerobic and resistance exercise, (2) aerobic and resistance exercise combined with neurodynamic interventions, or (3) a wait-list control group.

The study aims to determine whether the addition of neurodynamic interventions provides additional benefit beyond exercise therapy alone with regard to CIPN symptoms, physical functioning, psychosocial functioning, and quality of life. Furthermore, the study will explore potential underlying mechanisms associated with symptom development and recovery.
interventions: Exercise program 2: aerobic + resistance training combined with neurodynamic exercises
primary_outcomes: Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) sensory symptom severity
title: The Effect of Aerobic and Resistance Training With and Without Neurodynamic Exercises on Chemotherapy-induced Peripheral Neuropathy Symptoms and Associated Neuro-immune Mechanisms

brief_summary:
Ulcerative colitis is a condition that causes inflammation and ulcers in the large intestine. MGT-006 is an investigational oral capsule containing viable gut microbiota from screened human donors. This study will evaluate the safety and tolerability of MGT-006 in adults with moderately active ulcerative colitis. It will also examine whether gut microbiota from MGT-006 engraft in participants' intestines and explore changes in ulcerative colitis symptoms and inflammation.

The study has two parts. In Phase 1b, participants will be randomly assigned to receive MGT-006 either without antibiotic pretreatment or after five days of oral vancomycin or AFM (Amoxicillin/Fosfomycin/Metronidazole) pretreatment. MGT-006 will be taken for eight weeks, followed by four weeks of observation. Phase 2a is planned to explore different doses and potentially different dosing regimens of MGT-006, using the pretreatment approach selected from Phase 1b. The final Phase 2a design will depend on the Phase 1b findings and will be specified in an amended protocol before Phase 2a begins.
interventions: Amoxicillin hydrate/ Fosfomycin calcium hydrate/ Metronidazole
primary_outcomes: Safety and tolerability of MGT-006 (adverse events, adverse reactions)
title: Safety, Dosage, and Microbiome Engraftment Study of MGT-006 for Ulcerative Colitis (ROOT Study)

brief_summary:
Aim: To determine the effect of an oral care procedure using cold distilled water, initiated in the preoperative period, on the level of discomfort associated with thirst in patients undergoing lung resection.

Methods: This randomized controlled study was conducted between December 12, 2024, and December 24, 2025 with the participation of a sample of 78 patients who undergoing lung surgery in the Thoracic Surgery Department of a University hospital. Patients who received oral care using cold distilled water at four-hour intervals starting from the time of hospital admission were included in the experimental group.
title: The Effect of Preoperative Oral Care Procedures on Postoperative Thirst Discomfort

brief_summary: This study investigates how OPTIMAL theory influences table tennis backhand learning in young, healthy older, and mild cognitively impaired older adults. Meanwhile, we investigate the neural mechanisms of motor skill acquisition across different ages. This study utilizes functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) to monitor brain activity. Beyond immediate performance, the research focuses on Retention (sustained skill over time) and Transfer (application to novel tasks) as critical indicators of true motor learning. To ensure objective results, a double-blind design is employed, where both participants and data analysts remain blinded to group assignments during behavioral and fNIRS data processing to minimize bias.
lead_sponsor: National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University
title: OPTIMAL Motor Learning in Table Tennis: A fNIRS Study

brief_summary: Parkinson's disease often causes constipation and changes in gut bacteria, but it is not known how quickly a daily fiber supplement changes gut physiology in people with Parkinson's, or how long any change lasts after stopping. This study will test how a daily fiber bar affects bowel function and gut inflammation in people with Parkinson's disease and in household members who live with them. Participants will eat one fiber bar (11 grams of fiber) each day for 3 months, then stop and be followed for one more month, for about 4 months in total. At three points (before starting, after 3 months of fiber, and one month after stopping), participants will collect a stool sample at home and mail it to Stanford in a provided kit, so no clinic visits are needed. Every week, participants will also fill out a short questionnaire about how often they have bowel movements, their bowel regimen, and they will complete a questionnaire about how bowel symptoms affect their daily life. In the lab, we will measure proteins in the stool that are signs of gut inflammation. We want to learn how fast these proteins change when fiber is added, whether changes last after fiber is stopped, and whether people with Parkinson's respond differently than their household partners. We expect that fiber will change gut inflammation and bowel function during the fiber period, and that these changes will differ between people with Parkinson's and their partners after the fiber bars are stopped. Results may help guide future research on diet and gut function in Parkinson's disease.
title: Stanford University Neurofiber Study

brief_summary: The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if Kuntai capsule works to treat perimenopausal symptoms caused by GnRH-a in adults. It will also learn about the safety of Kuntai capsule.
title: Clinical Study on the Efficacy and Safety of Heyan® Kuntai Capsules in Alleviating Perimenopausal Symptoms Induced by GnRH-a

brief_summary: This is a Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, active- and placebo-controlled, multicenter inpatient study to examine the efficacy and safety of HS-10380 in adult Participants who are acutely psychotic with a Diagnostic and Statistical Manual Fifth Edition (DSM-5) diagnosis of schizophrenia. The primary objective of the study is to assess the efficacy of HS-10380 versus placebo in reducing Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS) total scores in adult inpatients with a DSM-5 diagnosis of schizophrenia. The secondary objectives of the study are to evaluate the response rate, improvement in disease severity and symptoms, safety and tolerability.
primary_outcomes: Change from Baseline in Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS) Total Score at Week 6 (Day 42)
title: Phase 3 Study of HS-10380 for Acute Schizophrenia in Chinese Adults

brief_summary:
Background: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) represents a growing global public health challenge, with rising prevalence in low and middle-income countries, including Bangladesh. Progressive renal dysfunction is frequently accompanied by gut microbiota alterations, leading to increased intestinal permeability and systemic inflammation through the gut-kidney axis. Accumulation of uremic toxins derived from dysbiotic microbiota has been implicated in CKD progression. Synbiotic therapy, combining probiotics and prebiotics, has been proposed as a strategy to restore microbial balance and reduce inflammatory burden.

Objective: To evaluate effect of Synbiotic Therapy on Renal Function Outcomes in Patients with Chronic Kidney Disease Stage III-IV.

Materials and Methods: This Double-blind, randomized placebo-controlled trial will be conducted in the Department of Nephrology, Chittagong Medical College Hospital, Bangladesh. Approximately 96 adult non-dialysis CKD stage III-IV patients will be enrolled. Participants will be randomly allocated into two arms of treatment. The experimental arm and the control arm. Both arm with receive standard care according to KDIGO recommendations. The experimental arm will receive synbiotic therapy and the control arm with receive placebo in addition to standard therapy. Clinical and laboratory assessments will be performed at baseline, after 1.5 months and after 3 months. Outcome measures are change in S. Creatinine, e-GFR, Blood Urea Nitrogen (BUN), C-Reactive protein (CRP), and Gastrointestinal symptom dynamics using Gastrointestinal System Rating Scale (GSRS).

Data Analysis Plan: An intention-to-treat or per protocol approach will be applied as applicable. Parametric or non-parametric tests will be applied as appropriate. Repeated-measures analysis will assess longitudinal changes.

Conclusion: The expected findings may clarify the potential role of gut microbiota modulation as an adjunct in CKD management in Bangladesh and similar settings and may inform future multicenter trials.
interventions: Experimental arm will get synbiotic therapy containing Lactobacillus acidophilus (15 billion CFU), Bifidobacterium longum (15 billion CFU), Streptococcus thermophilus(15 billion CFU), along with xylo
primary_outcomes: Change in Serum Creatinine From Baseline to 3 Months
Change in Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate (eGFR) From Baseline to 3 Months
Change in Blood Urea Nitrogen (BUN) From Baseline to 3 Months
title: Effect of Synbiotic Therapy on Renal Function Outcomes in Patients With Chronic Kidney Disease Stage III-IV: A Double-blind Randomized Placebo-controlled Trial.

brief_summary: Malaria cases are increasing in Papua New Guinea, partly because insecticide-treated nets do not fully protect people, especially from mosquitoes that bite outdoors. Spatial emanators are new devices that release insecticide into the air to repel or kill mosquitoes. This study will test whether these devices reduce malaria infections in rural villages in Madang Province by comparing households using indoor or outdoor devices with those without them. The results will help guide national malaria control strategies.
lead_sponsor: Macfarlane Burnet Institute for Medical Research and Public Health Ltd
title: Three-arm Cluster Randomised Control Trial Evaluation of Guardian Spatial Emanator as a Complimentary Vector Control Tool in Papua New Guinea

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether a 6-week mobile-delivered intervention combining mindfulness meditation (Headspace) and personalized, wearable-derived physical activity goals (Oura Ring) can be feasibly delivered to young people who are 1-5 years post-anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) and who have elevated fear of reinjury. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Can the Mind in Motion intervention be implemented with acceptable rates of recruitment, retention, engagement (mindfulness session completion, Oura Ring wear), and participant-rated acceptability?
* On days following a completed mindfulness session, do participants report lower anticipated fear of movement and show higher objectively measured moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA), compared with other days?

Participants will:

* Complete two brief in-person visits (approximately 1 week apart) that frame a 6-week home-based intervention period, followed by a remote assessment 4 weeks after the intervention ends.
* Wear a research-grade activPAL accelerometer on the thigh for 7 days before and 7 days after the intervention to measure objective physical activity.
* During the 6-week intervention, complete five 10-minute Headspace mindfulness sessions per week, wear an Oura Ring daily to receive personalized daily activity goals, and complete brief twice-daily check-ins (ecological momentary assessments) about fear, mood, and activity.
* Complete standard questionnaires about injury-related fear, psychological readiness for activity, and knee function/symptoms at baseline, mid-intervention, immediately after the intervention, and at a 4-week follow-up.
* Complete a brief audio-recorded exit interview describing their experience with the intervention.

This is a single-arm, single-site feasibility study; there is no control group and no randomization. Findings will inform the design of a future multisite randomized controlled trial.
title: Feasibility of a Mindfulness and Physical Activity Promotion Intervention After Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction

brief_summary: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a degenerative joint condition that causes pain, stiffness, reduced proprioception, impaired balance, and decreased physical function. This study aims to compare the effects of Dual Task Training and Rhythmic Stabilization Training on balance, proprioception, and physical function in patients with KOA. A randomized clinical trial will be conducted using convenient sampling, with participants randomly allocated into two groups. Both groups will receive a 15-minute hot pack followed by their respective interventions, three times per week for six weeks,12 sessions.
lead_sponsor: University of Management and Technology Lahore
primary_outcomes: Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index:
title: Comparative Effect of Dual Task Training and Rhythmic Stabilization in Knee Osteoarthritis Patients

brief_summary:
This clinical trial will test a Mindful Self-Compassion (MSC) group program after breast cancer treatment. MSC teaches people to notice difficult feelings and respond to themselves with kindness.

The study will enroll 80 adults aged 20 years or older. They must have completed their main breast cancer treatment within 12 months before enrollment.

The main questions are:

* Does MSC support psychological growth after cancer? This includes appreciating life, closer relationships, new possibilities, personal strength, and spiritual changes.
* Does MSC lower emotional distress, including anxiety and depression?
* Do changes in self-compassion, repetitive thoughts, and ways of handling emotions help explain these effects?

Researchers will compare MSC plus usual care with usual care alone during a waiting period. They expect the MSC group to report greater psychological growth and less emotional distress.

Cheng Ching General Hospital will help recruit participants and explain the study before obtaining written consent.

The study will recruit participants in two cohorts of 40 people each. Within each cohort, participants will join the MSC group or waitlist group by chance. Each participant has an equal chance of joining either group. Each cohort will include 20 participants in each group. Across both cohorts, there will be 40 participants in each group.

Participants in the MSC group will:

* Attend one live online 105-minute group session each week for eight weeks.
* Take part in mindfulness exercises, self-compassion practices, writing, and group discussions.
* Be encouraged to practice these skills at home.

Both groups will continue their usual medical and psychological care. Both groups will complete questionnaires at three times:

* Before the eight-week program begins.
* At the end of the eight-week program.
* Three months after the program ends.

The waitlist group will continue usual care without the study's MSC program during these assessments. After completing the three-month follow-up questionnaires, they can choose to attend the MSC program.
primary_outcomes: Change in Psychological Distress Measured by the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale
Change in Posttraumatic Growth Inventory-Short Form Score
title: Effects of a Mindful Self-Compassion Intervention on Psychological Adjustment in Breast Cancer Survivors

brief_summary:
This study investigated the effects of inspiratory muscle training (IMT) combined with aerobic exercise on diaphragm function, disease activity, functional exercise capacity, fatigue, sleep quality, and health-related quality of life in patients with axial spondyloarthritis (AxSpA).

Axial spondyloarthritis is a chronic inflammatory rheumatic disease that primarily affects the spine and sacroiliac joints. Reduced chest wall mobility and respiratory muscle function may contribute to decreased exercise capacity, fatigue, and impaired quality of life.

This randomized controlled trial was conducted at Bursa Yuksek Ihtisas Training and Research Hospital, Türkiye, between May 2023 and March 2024. Forty-two male patients aged 18-60 years were randomly allocated to two groups.

The control group received aerobic exercise and conventional spinal mobility exercises, while the intervention group received additional inspiratory muscle training using a respiratory resistance device. Both groups participated in a 12-week exercise program.

Participants were assessed at baseline and after 12 weeks using diaphragm ultrasonography, disease activity measures, functional exercise tests, and validated questionnaires assessing fatigue, sleep quality, and quality of life.

The study aimed to determine whether adding inspiratory muscle training to an aerobic exercise program provides additional clinical benefits for patients with axial spondyloarthritis.
lead_sponsor: Bursa Yuksek Ihtisas Training and Research Hospital
primary_outcomes: Change in Right Diaphragmatic End-Inspiratory Thickness
Change in Left Diaphragmatic End-Inspiratory Thickness
Change in Ankylosing Spondylitis Disease Activity Score with C-Reactive Protein (ASDAS-CRP)
Change in Six-Minute Walk Test Distance (6MWT)
title: Inspiratory Muscle Training in Axial Spondyloarthritis

brief_summary:
A transverse patellar fracture is a break across the kneecap that can affect knee movement, walking, and daily activities. Surgery is often needed to restore the position of the broken bone and allow it to heal.

This study will compare two surgical techniques for treating transverse patellar fractures in adults: K-wire tension band wiring and transosseous suture fixation using No. 5 FiberWire. The purpose is to determine whether the two techniques differ in knee function, fracture healing, and the occurrence of complications.

Eligible adults with an acute, closed transverse patellar fracture will be randomly assigned to one of the two treatment groups. Participants will be followed for 12 months after surgery. Knee function will be assessed using the Bostman score, while other outcomes will include pain, knee range of motion, quadriceps muscle strength, fracture healing, and complications such as infection, hardware irritation, and the need for further surgery.

The findings may help improve understanding of the benefits and limitations of these two surgical techniques and support clinical decision-making for adults with transverse patellar fractures.
primary_outcomes: Functional Outcome Assessed Using the Böstman Patellar Fracture Score at 12 Months
title: Comparison of Functional Results and Complications Between K-Wire Tension Band Fixation and Interosseous Suturing in Transverse Patellar Fractures: A Randomized Controlled Trial

brief_summary: This study tested whether a 12-week supervised multicomponent exercise program is associated with changes in blood pressure, estimated cardiorespiratory fitness, handgrip strength and health-related quality of life in women aged 45 to 59 years with hypertension. The program combined strength training, aerobic exercise (brisk walking or light jogging), controlled breathing and flexibility, in three sessions per week of about 60 minutes, mainly in community spaces in Bogotá, Colombia, with a hybrid option for women who could not attend in person. Thirty-two women were assigned, by convenience according to their availability for the class schedule, to an exercise group (n = 16) or to a control group that kept its usual activities (n = 16). Systolic and diastolic blood pressure, estimated cardiorespiratory fitness (Rockport 1-mile walk test), handgrip strength (dynamometer) and quality of life (SF-36 questionnaire) were measured before and after the 12 weeks.
primary_outcomes: Change in resting systolic blood pressure (SBP) from baseline to week 12
Change in resting diastolic blood pressure (DBP) from baseline to week 12
title: Multicomponent Exercise Program in Women With Hypertension

brief_summary: The purpose of the study is to test whether low-level electric stimulation, called High Definition transcranial Direct Current Stimulation (HDtDCS), on the part of the brain (i.e., left inferior frontal gyrus) thought to aid in memory will improve verbal retrieval in multiple sclerosis patients. The primary outcome measures are neuropsychological assessments of verbal retrieval, and the secondary measures are neuropsychological assessments of other cognitive abilities and electroencephalography (EEG) measures.
interventions: High Definition transcranial Direct Current Stimulation
Sham High Definition transcranial Direct Current Stimulation
lead_sponsor: The University of Texas at Dallas
primary_outcomes: Treatment group differences in change from baseline to 2-months post-treatment for Period 1 in Category Fluency
Treatment group differences in change from 2-months post-treatment for Period 1 to 2-months post-treatment for Period 2 in Category Fluency
Treatment group differences in change from baseline to 2-months post-treatment for Period 1 in Verbal Fluency
Treatment group differences in change from 2-months post-treatment for Period 1 to 2-months post-treatment for Period 2 in Verbal Fluency
title: Treatment of Memory Retrieval Impairments in MS With HDtDCS to the LIFG in a Placebo Controlled Trial

brief_summary: Current methods of measuring the response to new treatments for muscular dystrophies involve the examination of small pieces of muscle tissue called biopsies. The investigators are interested in finding less invasive methods that reduce the need for muscle biopsies. The purpose of this research is to learn about the possibility of detecting and measuring the activity and severity of myotonic dystrophy by examining a urine sample and a blood sample, and performing muscle function testing. The information that is gathered from this study may help to evaluate, prevent, diagnose, treat, and improve the understanding of human myotonic dystrophy.
title: Metabolomic Biomarkers of Myotonic Dystrophy

brief_summary: Rates of suicide among Canadian youth have risen steadily over the past two decades, alongside rapid growth in social media use-especially TikTok. Our research shows that TikTok contains substantial suicide-related content that may pose risks to vulnerable young people by provoking distress or encouraging copycat behaviour. Many creators add trigger warnings (TWs) to flag upsetting material, yet their impact is unclear. Although research shows mixed effects of TWs among people with trauma histories, no studies have examined TWs in the context of suicide-related content. Our recent findings indicate that TWs are associated with reduced engagement suicide-related videos on TikTok-contrary to our hypothesis that they might increase engagement. Although we can only speculate, reduced engagement may reflect youth avoiding TW-labelled content, or other unknown factors. This study will examine how a clinical population of youth at risk of suicide emotionally and behaviourally respond to TWs on self-harm and suicide-related content. Findings will provide key evidence to inform public health recommendations aimed at protecting youth from harmful content online.
title: Exploring The Effect of TikTok Trigger Warnings in a Clinical Sample of Youth at Risk of Suicide

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate if multi-dose fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) capsules can safely and effectively slow down biological aging and reduce chronic low-grade inflammation in adults aged 45 to 80 with metabolic neglect.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Can oral FMT capsules significantly slow the biological pace of aging as measured by the DunedinPACE epigenetic clock?
* Can FMT successfully reduce chronic systemic inflammation (measured by markers such as suPAR, IL-6, and hs-CRP)?

Researchers will compare participants receiving the active product to those receiving a matching placebo to see if the microbiome intervention improves metabolic health and cognitive function via the gut-brain axis.

Participants will:

* Undergo a short-term preparation phase involving targeted antibiotics and standard bowel cleansing.
* Receive an 2 initial induction doses of active product (or placebo) followed by 5 regular booster cycles administered approximately every 4 weeks.
* Attend periodic clinical visits for physical examinations, blood draws, stool sample collection (at home), and cognitive testing using the CANTAB platform and MoCA scale.
* Maintain a participant diary to record adverse events (AE), product administration, stool sample collection, and dietary habits.
interventions: Fecal microbiota transplantation delivery through oral capsules (HBI MBiotix Caps)
PLACEBO for Fecal microbiota delivery through oral capsules
primary_outcomes: Percentage of Participants Achieving Clinical and Biological Response (Responder Rate)
title: Fecal Microbiota Transplantation (FMT) to Slow Biological Aging

brief_summary: Chronic non-specific neck pain (CNNP) is a common musculoskeletal disorder associated with persistent pain, functional disability, and reduced quality of life. Manual therapy techniques such as Maitland mobilization and multimodal manual therapy are frequently used in physiotherapy; however, evidence directly comparing their effectiveness remains limited. This study aims to compare the effects of Multimodal Manual Therapy and Maitland Mobilization on pain intensity, functional disability, and quality of life in patients with chronic non-specific neck pain. A randomized clinical trial will be conducted at Life Care Hospital, Bahawalnagar, involving 54 participants aged 18-35 years who meet the inclusion criteria. Participants will be randomly allocated into two equal groups. Group A will receive Maitland mobilization, while Group B will receive Multimodal Manual Therapy, including high thoracic manipulation (T4), cervical mobilization, and suboccipital muscle inhibition. Both groups will receive treatment three times per week for four weeks. Outcome measures will include the Numeric Pain Rating Scale (NPRS) for pain, the Neck Disability Index (NDI) for functional disability, and the Short Form-12 (SF-12) questionnaire for quality of life. Assessments will be performed at baseline, the second week, and the fourth week. Data will be analyzed using SPSS version 24, with appropriate parametric or non-parametric statistical tests based on data distribution. The findings of this study are expected to identify the more effective intervention for improving pain, disability, and quality of life in individuals with chronic non-specific neck pain. The results may assist physiotherapists in selecting evidence-based treatment strategies and contribute to improving clinical management of this condition
lead_sponsor: University of Management and Technology Lahore
primary_outcomes: PAIN BY NUMERIC PAIN RATING SCALE
Physical and mental health SHORT FORM 12-ITEM SURVEY (SF-12)
title: Multimodal Manual Therapy vs. Maitland Mobilization for Chronic Non-Specific Neck Pain

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if balance training on a moving (dynamic) platform with visual and sound feedback, combined with weak electrical brain stimulation, helps people recover balance and movement after an ischemic stroke with weakness on one side of the body (hemiparesis).

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does the combination of dynamic platform training and active brain stimulation improve balance more than either method alone?
* Does it improve independence in daily activities, mobility and walking, and reduce fall risk?
* Is the combined treatment safe in the early period after stroke? Researchers will compare four groups: dynamic platform training with active stimulation, dynamic platform training with sham (imitation) stimulation, training on a locked (static) platform with active stimulation, and training on a locked platform with sham stimulation.

Participants will:

* Receive standard rehabilitation (exercise therapy and physiotherapy) of the same volume in all groups.
* Complete 10 sessions of 20-minute platform training over 12 days (5 sessions per week), with active or sham brain stimulation during each session.
* Have balance, mobility and neurological tests on Day 0, Day 6 and Day 12.
primary_outcomes: Change from Baseline in Berg Balance Scale (BBS)
title: Dynamic Stabilometry Combined With Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation for Balance and Motor Recovery After Ischemic Stroke

brief_summary:
Study Description As most clinical trials in Alzheimer's disease (AD) have been unsuccessful to date, it has become increasingly crucial to focus on treating earlier stages of the disease. Compelling evidence indicates that sleep disruption is associated with accumulation of Alzheimer's biomarkers, including amyloid-beta (Aβ) and tau pathology. Slow-wave activity (SWA) during sleep is particularly important for the clearance of Aβ and sleep-dependent memory consolidation, and sleep disturbance could reduce the amount of time spent in slow-wave sleep. Together, these findings suggest that treating sleep disruption in older adults may help reduce the level of adverse brain aging.

The goal of this study is to better understand the effect of sleep interventions on improving sleep and building cognitive resilience in older adults with amnestic mild cognitive impairment (aMCI), and to assess the feasibility of relevant study protocols. Fifty older adults (ages 60-85) with aMCI and sleep disturbance (Insomnia Severity Index score of 8 or greater) will be randomized 1:1 to one of two treatment arms: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia only (CBT-I + Sham), or CBT-I combined with acoustic slow-wave activity enhancement (CBT-I + SWAE). CBT-I is a psychotherapy intervention designed to address maladaptive cognitive and behavioral patterns associated with sleep and bedtime. SWAE is administered through non-invasive earbuds (Smartbuds, NextSense Inc.) that detect and amplify endogenous slow-wave activity using acoustic pulses during sleep.

Each participant will complete 3 visits over approximately 6 months: a baseline visit, a post-treatment visit (approximately 12 weeks after baseline), and a 6-month follow-up visit. Group differences will be compared on changes in cognitive performance and plasma biomarkers of AD (phosphorylated tau \[pTau-217\]) across these time points. The study will also explore potential mechanisms behind the relationship between sleep and cognition/biomarkers by investigating a range of objectively measured sleep metrics (e.g., sleep architecture, sleep duration, arousals) along with depressive symptoms.

Hypotheses:

CBT-I will be associated with more favorable outcomes (i.e., less decline or greater improvement) in frontal network functioning (sustained attention/target detection, executive functions), while SWAE will be associated with better outcomes in measures of episodic memory (word-list learning and story recall). Improvements in total sleep time and insomnia symptoms at 8 weeks are hypothesized to mediate the relationship between CBT-I and performance on attention and executive functions over 6 months, while improvements in slow-wave non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep at 12 weeks are hypothesized to mediate the relationship between SWAE and episodic memory measures. Additionally, CBT-I is hypothesized to be associated with increased scores on the Visuospatial Abilities, Planning, Organization, and Divided Attention subscales of the Everyday Cognition (ECog) questionnaire after 6 months, while SWAE is hypothesized to be associated with a significant increase in the Everyday Memory subscale.

Objectives:

Aim 1: To determine if CBT-I and SWAE have different neuropsychological outcomes in aMCI.

Aim 2: To examine the impact of sleep treatments on cognitively mediated everyday functioning.

Exploratory Aim: To assess whether CBT-I and/or SWAE are associated with changes in plasma pTau and whether pTau moderates the association between sleep and cognition.

Results from this study will determine whether sleep interventions can build brain and cognitive resilience in the context of aging, and will inform the design of a future, larger-scale R01 study rigorously examining the association between targeted sleep modifications and markers of AD pathophysiology as a potentially modifiable risk factor for dementia.
primary_outcomes: Change in Attention/Executive Function Composite Score
title: Targeting Sleep and Slow-Wave Activity to Enhance Cognition in MCI

brief_summary:
Current practice and debate: Many medical schools use hybrid models that combine modular and final exams to balance reliability, validity, and feasibility. Still, there is no consensus on the optimal structure. The debate centers on three issues: educational impact, student stress, and faculty workload. Modular systems may support continuous learning but raise concerns about assessment burden and fragmentation of knowledge, as students may learn topics in isolation rather than as an integrated whole. End-of-term exams, by contrast, risk encouraging short-term memorization even though they test integration more effectively.

Justification for the study: Given these competing advantages and drawbacks, the study aims to explore the perspectives of both students and faculty on the two approaches. Understanding how each stakeholder group perceives the effects on learning, stress, workload, and performance can fill a gap in the existing literature, which focuses mainly on learning behaviors rather than stakeholder views.

Expected contribution: The findings are intended to inform evidence-based decisions on assessment design in preclinical medical education. By clarifying the trade-offs between distributed and cumulative exams, the study seeks to help institutions optimize learning outcomes while keeping assessment workload and student stress manageable
primary_outcomes: To compare student and faculty satisfaction and perceived effectiveness between the vertical (end-of-term) examination system used in Year 1 and the horizontal (end-of-module) examination system used in Year 2 among undergraduate medical students
title: End of Term vs. End of Module Examinations in the Preclinical Stage: A Cross-Sectional Survey of Student and Faculty Perspectives

brief_summary: The purpose of this pilot randomized, wait-list controlled study is to evaluate the effects of exercise dose in terms of frequency (1 vs. 2 days per week) in individuals on systemic treatment for colorectal cancer. The impact on the individual (physical function, quality of life, fatigue and other patient reported outcomes) as well as on health care utilization (cost to deliver, cost to individuals, savings and impact to the health care system) will be evaluated. In addition, assessments of immunological markers to better understand the biological impact of exercise dose on immunological markers will be explored.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of patients in the once per week and twice per week group that achieve an increase of ≥10 MET-h/wk of total physical activity level at 12 weeks.
title: Alberta Cancer Exercise Dose in Colorectal Cancer

brief_summary: End-Stage Kidney Disease (ESKD) in children is a severe and irreversible condition that significantly impacts their growth, development, and overall quality of life. Children with ESKD often face numerous physical, emotional, and social challenges, including the need for life-saving dialysis or kidney transplantation. Despite advancements in clinical management, dietary adherence remains a critical component in managing ESKD and improving health outcomes. This study will compare two approaches to providing medically tailored meals (MTMs) for children with ESKD. A total of 30 children and their parents or caregivers will be randomly assigned to one of two groups: (1) a culinary medicine program that teaches families how to plan, shop for, and prepare kidney-friendly meals at home, or (2) a program that provides pre-prepared, kidney-friendly meals delivered to their homes. The study will assess how practical and acceptable each approach is for families and examine its potential effects on children's health and dietary habits. Researchers will evaluate participation, satisfaction, and study completion rates. They will also examine changes in children's blood potassium and phosphorus levels, blood pressure, fluid balance, diet quality, and health-related quality of life. In addition, the study will explore whether the culinary medicine program improves parents' nutrition knowledge, confidence in preparing healthy meals, meal planning, grocery shopping, cooking skills, and availability of healthy foods at home. Researchers will also compare the costs of the two approaches, including food, educational materials, and staff time, to estimate the cost per child. The findings will help determine whether these approaches are practical for families and provide information to guide future studies and programs to improve nutrition and health among children with ESKD.
title: Comparative Feasibility and Effectiveness of Medically Tailored Meals Approaches for Pediatric End-Stage Kidney Disease

brief_summary: This randomised controlled trial tests whether a structured six-pillar lifestyle medicine programme can lead to remission of type 2 diabetes in adults in Lahore, Pakistan. The programme combines a plant-predominant eating pattern without calorie counting, adapted to local Pakistani foods, with physical activity, sleep, stress regulation, social connection and reduced exposure to risky substances. Adults aged 30 to 65 years with type 2 diabetes of up to 8 years' duration, managed on oral medication only, are randomised to the programme or to usual care. The primary outcome is remission at 6 months, defined as HbA1c below 6.5% sustained for at least three months without glucose-lowering medication.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of participants achieving type 2 diabetes remission
title: Lifestyle Medicine for Type 2 Diabetes Remission in Pakistan

brief_summary: This clinical study is designed to explore the safety and tolerability of UX-DA003. It will also explore if UX-DA003 works to improve motor function in subjects with Parkinson's disease.
lead_sponsor: The First Affiliated Hospital of Anhui Medical University
primary_outcomes: Incidence and severity of adverse events (AEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs)
title: Exploratory Clinical Trial of UX-DA003 Injection for the Treatment of Patients With Parkinson's Disease

brief_summary: Total knee arthroplasty (TKA) is a cost effective solution for people with end-stage knee osteoarthritis. Given Hong Kong's large senior population and age as the primary risk factor for osteoarthritis, waiting times for total knee arthroplasty can reach 30 months. To manage this long wait list, patients would be enrolled to a structured exercise program with group and home based exercise. Currently limited options are available for home based exercise adherence monitoring for TKA patients on the wait-list. This study will assess the effect of wearable device with smartphone application to guide home based exercise among these wait-list patients. The main hypothesis is that the use of wearable device will decrease patient's pain level and improve their physical activity level.
title: Wearable Device Guided Exercise for Patients on Total Knee Arthroplasty Wait-list

brief_summary:
The China HEalthy Aging and Dementia (HEAD) study is a large-scale, community-based, multi-center prospective cohort study covering eastern, northern, southern, and central-western regions of China. By integrating comprehensive clinical, neuroimaging, biospecimen, and multi-omics data, the study aims to advance the early prediction and diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease and related dementias (ADRD) and provide a foundation for future intervention studies in the Chinese population.

The primary aims of the China HEAD study are as follows:

1. To establish a community-based prospective cohort by recruiting over 20,000 participants from eastern, northern, southern, western, and middle regions of China.
2. To build a comprehensive biobank by collecting demographic information, disease history, cognitive function, physical measures, electrophysiologic data, multimodal imaging data, as well as biospecimens and derived multi-omics data.
3. To conduct early prediction and diagnosis studies for ADRD and support future intervention studies based on the above-mentioned cohort and biobank.
primary_outcomes: Mild cognitive impairment due to Alzheimer's disease (MCI due to AD)
Dementia due to Alzheimer's disease (AD dementia)
Clinical Dementia Rating Scale Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB) score
title: China HEalthy Aging and Dementia Study (HEAD)

brief_summary: Rehabilitation remains important in the chronic phase after stroke or spinal cord injury, as meaningful improvements may still be achieved through intensive, goal-directed, and personalized training. INTeRAcT-bis is a follow-up study of the original INTeRAcT program, which consisted of a 3-week intensive rehabilitation intervention (90 therapy hours) combining conventional therapy, goal-directed training, self-management, and advanced rehabilitation technologies. The study has two main objectives: (1) to evaluate the long-term clinical and health economic effects of the original INTeRAcT program, and (2) to assess the clinical effects and implementation of a second intensive rehabilitation period ("boost"). Participants receive a personalized 3-week rehabilitation program targeting upper and/or lower limb impairments based on their individual goals. In addition to clinical and health economic outcomes, the study examines participant experiences and implementation factors to support a broader implementation of intensive rehabilitation in the future.
primary_outcomes: Change in Spinal Cord Independence Measure (SCIM)
title: Long-Term Clinical, Health Economic, and Process Evaluation of Intensive Technology-Integrated Motor Rehabilitation in Chronic Neurological Conditions (INTeRAcT-bis)

brief_summary: This study will compare speech understanding in noise using a remote microphone with hearing aids and compatible receivers with speech understanding in noise using hearing aids alone in a population of hearing impaired adults, age 18 and over. Participants will be tested in a near condition (target speech and remote microphone located 1 meter away from participant) as well as a far condition (target speech and remote microphone located 2 meters away from participant). Subjective questionnaire about listening effort and overall satisfaction will also be administered to each participant.
interventions: Commercially available Receiver in the Canal (RIC) hearing devices
Hearing Aids plus Remote Microphone System
title: Performance of a Remote Microphone Compared to Hearing Aids Alone

brief_summary: Pneumonia is a common respiratory infection in children that may cause respiratory distress and impaired oxygenation. This quasi-experimental study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of nurse-directed therapeutic positioning on vital signs, oxygen saturation, and respiratory distress severity among children aged 3-5 years diagnosed with pneumonia. The study will compare two therapeutic positioning interventions, side-lying position and semi-Fowler's position, with a control group receiving routine nursing care. The outcomes will be assessed to determine the effects of these positioning interventions on the respiratory status of children with pneumonia.
title: Effect of Nurse-Directed Therapeutic Positioning in Children With Pneumonia

brief_summary: This study will investigate the acute effect of a single session of moderate-intensity aerobic exercise on blood pressure responses to mental stress in teachers. Participants will complete two experimental sessions: a control session without exercise and a 30-minute moderate-intensity aerobic exercise session. The intensity of the aerobic exercise session will be set at 50-60% of the heart rate reserve. The order of the experimental sessions will be randomized. We will assess blood pressure and heart rate at rest and during a mental stress test performed before and 30 minutes after each session. The two sessions will be separated by 48-72 hours.
primary_outcomes: Systolic blood pressure reactivity to mental stress
title: Acute Effect of Aerobic Exercise on Cardiovascular Reactivity During a Mental Stress Test in Teachers

brief_summary: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) is a progressive respiratory condition characterized by airflow limitation, dyspnea, and fatigue, significantly impairing quality of life. Globally, COPD is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality, with its burden disproportionately affecting low- and middle-income countries such as Pakistan, where healthcare resources are limited and structured rehabilitation programs are scarce. Despite evidence supporting pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) as an effective intervention for improving physical capacity, symptom control, and quality of life, its implementation in Pakistan remains minimal. Nurse-led PR programs, which integrate education, and exercise have demonstrated positive outcomes internationally; however, their feasibility and effectiveness in resource-limited settings are largely unexplored. Thus, the aim of this study is to assess the impact of a nurse-led PR program in improving dyspnea, fatigue and self-efficacy in patients with COPD. Adults (aged ≥40 years) meeting eligibility criteria will be randomly allocated to an intervention or control group. Prior to the start of the intervention, baseline data will be collected from both groups using Modified Medical Research Council Dyspnea, Fatigue Severity and COPD Self-Efficacy Scales to assess the severity of dyspnea, fatigue and level of COPD self-efficacy. The intervention group will be provided with a nurse-led structured PR program by the researcher which will include COPD education, breathing and strengthening exercises for 12 weeks. The first sessions will be conducted during outpatient visits and will be followed up by weekly telephonic reminders and bi-weekly face-to-face meet-up to ensure continued adherence and individualized guidance. While, the control group will receive standard care which include routine medical management. After completion of 12-week intervention, the same scales will be used to evaluate changes in the outcome variables i.e. dyspnea, fatigue and COPD self-efficacy. Descriptive statistics will be used to summarize the demographic and clinical characteristics. To evaluate the effectiveness of the pulmonary rehabilitation program on dyspnea and fatigue status, Chi-square / Fisher's exact test will be used to compare the post-intervention results between the two groups. Independent sample t-test / Mann-Whitney test will be used to compare the self-efficacy score between the intervention and control groups. The findings of this study are expected to provide empirical evidence of the effectiveness of nurse-led pulmonary rehabilitation and inform evidence-based healthcare policies. The findings may also support the integration of nurse-led PR into routine COPD care as a feasible, cost-effective strategy to improve symptom management and quality of life among patients with COPD.
title: Impact of Nurse-Led Pulmonary Rehabilitation on Dyspnea, Fatigue and Self-Efficacy in COPD Patients

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to investigate the relationship between non-invasive brain monitoring measurements and neurological recovery six months after cardiac arrest in patients admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU).

After admission to the ICU, patients who have had a cardiac arrest will undergo non-invasive brain monitoring. Six months later, their neurological outcome will be assessed using a telephone interview with the patient or their caregiver.

Based on this assessment, patients will be classified as having either a good or poor neurological outcome. The study will then investigate whether the brain monitoring measurements can help distinguish between these two groups.
title: Continuous Noninvasive Multimodal Neuromonitoring at the ICU After Cardiac Arrest

brief_summary: Tramadol is commonly used postoperatively due to its ease of administration, but it carries several risks, including interindividual variability, drug interactions, neuropsychiatric risks in elderly patients, and long-term dependence. Although its analgesic efficacy is comparable to that of strong opioids, its role in a multimodal analgesia strategy remains insufficiently studied. Research tailored to current clinical practices is needed to accurately assess its tolerance profile.
title: Tramadol Versus Morphine for Postoperative Pain Relief Following Laparoscopic Abdominal Surgery

brief_summary:
Cervical length, measured via transvaginal ultrasound, changes as pregnancy progresses. However, reference information for interpreting cervical length measurements during late pregnancy in Vietnam remains limited. This study aims to describe gestational-age-specific cervical length percentiles in a selected population of women with singleton pregnancies receiving care at My Duc Hospital.

The study plans to enroll 294 women who have a documented cervical length greater than 25 mm between 16 weeks 0 days and 24 weeks 0 days of gestation. Participants will be recruited between 28 weeks 0 days and 33 weeks 6 days of gestation.

Each participant may undergo up to three cervical length assessments during scheduled antenatal visits, occurring approximately two weeks apart: from 28 weeks 0 days to 29 weeks 6 days, from 30 weeks 0 days to 31 weeks 6 days, and from 32 weeks 0 days to 33 weeks 6 days. No separate research-only visit is planned. At each assessment, the sonographer will obtain at least three technically acceptable measurements and will record the shortest measurement.

These measurements will be used to estimate cervical length percentiles by gestational age. Participants will also be followed through delivery, and pregnancy and newborn outcomes will be obtained from medical records. This study is observational and will not assign treatments or alter routine clinical care.
title: Cervical Length Reference Range at 28-34 Weeks in Singleton Pregnancies

brief_summary: This study is evaluating a new eye drop containing pregabalin (TB0001) as a potential treatment for people with primary open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension. The study aims to determine whether TB0001 lowers eye pressure as effectively as timolol, a commonly used glaucoma eye drop, while remaining safe and well tolerated. Participants will be randomly assigned to receive one of three strengths of TB0001 or timolol for 28 days. Eye pressure, eye health, side effects and tolerability will be assessed throughout the study. The results will help identify the most appropriate dose of TB0001 for future clinical studies.
primary_outcomes: Change from mean diurnal baseline IOP to mean diurnal IOP at Day 28
title: A Phase 2a Study Comparing the Efficacy, Safety and Tolerability of Pregabalin Eye Drops Comparing With Timolol Eye Drops in Adults With Glaucoma or High Eye Pressure.

brief_summary: This study aims to compare the effects of a laryngeal mask airway (i-gel) and an endotracheal tube on perioperative hypothermia in patients undergoing laparoscopic inguinal hernia surgery. The primary outcome is the incidence of hypothermia, defined as a core body temperature below 36°C, at the end of surgery. The study will also evaluate perioperative temperature changes and relevant postoperative outcomes between the two airway management groups.
lead_sponsor: Sultan Abdulhamid Han Training and Research Hospital, Istanbul, Turkey
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Perioperative Hypothermia at the End of Surgery
title: Effect of Laryngeal Mask Airway vs Endotracheal Tube on Hypothermia in Laparoscopic Hernia Surgery

brief_summary: This randomized, sham-controlled study investigated the acute effects of shoulder Dynamic Tape on serve velocity, isometric shoulder rotator muscle strength, functional throwing performance, and athlete satisfaction in competitive volleyball players. Thirty athletes aged 18-35 years were randomly assigned to a Dynamic Tape group (n = 15) or a sham taping group (n = 15). In both groups, serve velocity, shoulder internal and external rotation strength, and functional throwing performance were assessed under taped and untaped conditions. The order of the assessment conditions was randomized to minimize order effects. Assessments under the taped condition were performed 45 minutes after tape application. Athlete satisfaction was evaluated following taping.
title: Acute Effects of Shoulder Dynamic Taping in Competitive Volleyball Players

brief_summary:
Steatotic liver disease (SLD) is the most common chronic liver disease and is associated with an increased risk of liver-related complications, cardiovascular disease, and malignancies. However, comprehensive prospective data on the clinical characteristics, disease progression, and management of patients with SLD in Austria remain limited.

The SLD-AT study is a multicenter, prospective, observational registry with an associated biobank aiming to characterize patients with suspected or confirmed SLD in Austria. The registry will collect longitudinal clinical, laboratory, imaging, and treatment-related data to investigate disease progression, clinical outcomes, and the prognostic value of non-invasive tests and biomarkers.

The study aims to enroll approximately 20,000 participants over a planned duration of 15 years.
primary_outcomes: Number of participants developing compensated advanced chronic liver disease (cACLD), as assessed by liver stiffness measurement using vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE) >=10 kPa
title: Steatotic Liver Disease in Austria - Prospective Registry With Biobank

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether briefly stopping blood flow to the upper arms with inflatable cuffs before exercise (called ischemic preconditioning, or IPC) can improve judo-specific grip and pulling performance in trained junior male judo athletes aged 17 to 19 years. The study will also look at how IPC affects blood pressure, heart rate, hand grip strength, how hard the exercise feels, and muscle soreness.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does IPC help athletes hang longer from a judo jacket (judogi) with bent arms, and do more pull-ups while holding the jacket? Does IPC increase the number of judo pulling movements (hikidashi uchi-komi) an athlete can do in 20 seconds? Does IPC change blood pressure, heart rate, hand grip strength, perceived effort, and muscle soreness before the tests, right after the tests, and after 30 minutes of rest?

Researchers will compare IPC with a sham (fake) cuff treatment to see if IPC improves performance and recovery. In the IPC session, cuffs on both upper arms are inflated to 50 mmHg above the athlete's resting systolic (upper) blood pressure, which briefly stops blood flow to the arms. A finger sensor (pulse oximeter) is used to check that blood flow has stopped. In the sham session, the same cuffs are inflated to only 20 mmHg, which does not block blood flow. Each athlete receives both treatments on different days, in a random order.

Participants will:

Visit the judo training hall 3 times, with 3 days between visits. At the first visit, have their height, body weight, and body composition measured and practice all tests and the cuff procedure.

At the second and third visits, rest while their blood pressure, heart rate, and hand grip strength are measured.

Receive either IPC or the sham treatment: 3 rounds of 5 minutes of cuff inflation followed by 5 minutes of rest, for 30 minutes in total.

Have their blood pressure and heart rate measured again, then do a standard warm-up.

Complete 3 judo tests with 10 minutes of rest between them: hanging from a judo jacket with bent arms for as long as possible, doing as many pull-ups as possible while holding the jacket, and pulling a partner off balance as many times as possible in 20 seconds.

Rate how hard the tests felt and how sore their muscles are, and have their heart rate and hand grip strength measured right after the tests and again after 30 minutes of rest.

Avoid hard exercise, caffeine, and alcohol for 24 hours before each visit, and keep their usual diet and sleep during the study.
title: Upper Body Ischemic Preconditioning and Judo Performance

brief_summary:
This is a Phase Ib/II clinical trial designed to evaluate the safety, tolerability, and preliminary efficacy of an arginine-restricted diet combined with standard neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy in patients with locally advanced middle/high rectal cancer.

Background: Standard neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy is the standard treatment for locally advanced rectal cancer to shrink tumors before surgery. However, the rate of complete tumor disappearance (pathological complete response) with standard treatment remains relatively low (around 10-20%). Arginine is an amino acid that supports tumor growth and immune escape. Preclinical studies and our previous Phase I trial (NCT07038044) suggest that restricting arginine in the diet can alter tumor metabolism and enhance the body's anti-tumor immune response.

Study Design: The study consists of two phases. Phase Ib is a single-arm safety run-in, where 6 patients will receive the arginine-restricted diet plus standard chemoradiotherapy.

Phase II is a randomized, open-label, controlled phase. Approximately 120 patients will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to either the experimental group or the control group. Neither the patient nor the doctor can choose the group.

Interventions:

Standard Treatment: All participants will receive standard CAPOX chemotherapy (oxaliplatin and capecitabine) and long-course radiotherapy.

Arginine-Restricted Diet: Patients in the experimental group will consume a specially formulated, nutritionally complete, arginine-restricted nutritional powder combined with specific low-arginine foods for 7-8 weeks during the radiotherapy period, replacing their normal diet. Patients in the control group will maintain a normal diet.

Objectives: The primary objective is to evaluate whether this dietary intervention can improve the complete response rate (including pathological complete response \[pCR\] and clinical complete response \[cCR\]) compared to standard treatment alone. Secondary objectives include assessing safety (adverse events), surgical outcomes (R0 resection rate), survival outcomes (event-free survival, progression-free survival, overall survival), and changes in nutritional and immune status.
primary_outcomes: Rate of Complete Response (pCR and cCR)
title: Arginine-Restricted Diet Combined With Chemoradiotherapy in Neoadjuvant Rectal Cancer: A Phase Ib/II Trial

brief_summary:
Breastfeeding is the optimal method of infant feeding and provides significant health benefits for both mothers and infants. However, nipple pain, tenderness, fissures, and other nipple-related problems are common during the early postpartum period and frequently lead to breastfeeding difficulties or early discontinuation. Although various interventions, including breast milk, lanolin, and hydrogel dressings, have been used to prevent nipple trauma, there is still no consensus regarding the most effective approach. Beeswax possesses moisturizing, antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, and wound-healing properties and may represent a safe and natural alternative for preventing nipple damage. However, evidence regarding the effectiveness of beeswax-based nipple protectors remains limited.

This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of a beeswax-based nipple protector compared with routine breast milk application in preventing nipple problems among postpartum breastfeeding mothers. The study will be conducted as a prospective, randomized controlled trial in a university hospital. Postpartum mothers who meet the inclusion criteria will be randomly assigned to either the intervention group, which will use a beeswax-based nipple protector, or the control group, which will receive routine breast milk application. Participants will be followed during the first 20 postpartum days.

Data will be collected using a descriptive information form, a breast assessment form, the Visual Analogue Scale for pain, and the Breastfeeding Self-Efficacy Scale-Short Form. Assessments will be performed at baseline and on postpartum days 10 and 20. Statistical analyses will be conducted using appropriate descriptive and comparative methods according to data distribution, and repeated measurements will be analyzed using longitudinal statistical models.

This study is expected to provide evidence regarding the effectiveness of a beeswax-based nipple protector in reducing nipple pain and trauma and improving breastfeeding self-efficacy.
title: Effect of Beeswax-Based Nipple Protector and Breast Milk on Nipple Problems

brief_summary: Cervical spinal cord injuries (SCI) are the most common form of spinal cord injuries within the veteran population. Losing arm function is a major concern with these injuries. Doctors often use a treatment called functional electrical stimulation (FES) during rehab sessions targeted at improving arm and hand function. For FES, clinicians places sticky pads on the skin over the muscles that need to move. A newer treatment, called transcutaneous spinal stimulation (TSS), places the pads on the skin over the spine instead. This study compares the two treatments in veterans with non-traumatic spinal cord injuries while they are in the hospital's rehab program. The main goal is to see how well each treatment improves arm and hand function, which is measured with the Capabilities of Upper Extremity Test. If TSS works well, it could help veterans regain more arm and hand function which may result in increased independence.

title: Functional Electrical Stimulation vs Transcutaneous Stimulation in Patients With Subacute Spinal Cord Injury
