brief_summary:
This study aims to examine the effect of a suicide scenario-based clinical simulation on nursing students' suicide care competency and suicide stigma levels. The study uses a single-group pre-test/post-test (quasi-experimental) design. Nursing students enrolled in a Mental Health and Psychiatric Nursing course at a foundation university in Istanbul, Türkiye, who have not previously participated in a similar simulation, are invited to take part.

Before the simulation, participants complete a set of questionnaires assessing their suicide care competency and attitudes toward suicide stigma. They then take part in a structured simulation session involving a standardized patient portraying a person with suicidal history and risk. The session includes a prebriefing phase, a 15-minute clinical encounter, and a 60-minute debriefing session guided by the PEARLS model. Immediately afterward, participants complete the same questionnaires again.

The purpose of the study is to determine whether simulation-based training improves nursing students' competency in caring for individuals at suicide risk and reduces stigmatizing attitudes toward suicide, and to contribute evidence on the use of simulation in psychiatric nursing education.
title: Effect of Clinical Simulation on Suicide Care Competency and Suicide Stigma Levels of Psychiatric Nursing Students

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) combined with a working-memory task can treat chronic pain and related emotional and cognitive problems after chemotherapy in adult cancer survivors. tDCS is a non-invasive and painless technique that uses a very weak electrical current, applied through two small electrodes on the head, to modulate the activity of certain brain areas. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does tDCS reduce chronic pain intensity after chemotherapy in cancer survivors?
* Does tDCS also reduce anxiety, depression, and cognitive problems, and improve the regulation of cortisol, a stress-related hormone?
* Are the effects on pain, anxiety, depression, cognitive problems, and cortisol sustained when treatment continues with a maintenance phase of up to 2 months?

Researchers will compare real tDCS to sham (placebo) tDCS, a look-alike procedure that does not deliver effective stimulation, to see if real tDCS works to reduce pain and improve these symptoms.

Participants will:

* Receive real or sham tDCS (assigned by chance) in 5 daily sessions over 1 week. Each session lasts 20 minutes: 10 minutes at rest and 10 minutes while doing a working-memory task
* If they did not respond to sham tDCS, be offered 5 additional daily sessions of real tDCS
* If they respond to treatment, continue with real tDCS twice a week for up to 2 months
* Complete assessments of pain, mood, memory, attention, and quality of life before treatment, after each phase, and during and at the end of the maintenance phase
* Collect saliva samples to measure cortisol
lead_sponsor: Instituto de investigación e innovación biomédica de Cádiz
primary_outcomes: Change in pain intensity (Visual Analogue Scale, VAS) after the acute phase
title: Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation for Chemotherapy-Related Chronic Pain in Cancer Survivors

brief_summary: This phase I trial studies the side effects and best dose of asciminib when given together with intrathecal (IT) chemotherapy, dexamethasone, vincristine, and blinatumomab (asciminib-based induction therapy) in treating patients with newly diagnosed Philadelphia chromosome-positive (Ph+) acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). Asciminib may stop the growth of cancer cells by blocking some of the enzymes needed for cell growth. Chemotherapy drugs, such as methotrexate and cytarabine, work in different ways to stop the growth of cancer cells, either by killing the cells, by stopping them from dividing, or by stopping them from spreading. Dexamethasone is in a class of medications called corticosteroids. It is used to reduce inflammation and lower the body's immune response to help lessen the side effects of chemotherapy drugs. Vincristine is in a class of medications called vinca alkaloids. It works by stopping cancer cells from growing and dividing and may kill them. Blinatumomab is a monoclonal antibody that may interfere with the ability of cancer cells to grow and spread. A monoclonal antibody is a type of protein that can bind to certain targets in the body, such as molecules that cause the body to make an immune response (antigens). Giving asciminib-based induction therapy may be safe, tolerable, and/or effective in treating patients with newly diagnosed Ph+ ALL.
conditions: B Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia With t(9;22)(q34.1;q11.2); BCR-ABL1
title: Asciminib-Based Induction Therapy for the Treatment of Newly Diagnosed Philadelphia Chromosome-Positive Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia

brief_summary: Patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) have an increased risk of lung cancer, potentially influenced by targeted therapies such as JAK inhibitors and biologics. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are key mediators of intercellular communication and may carry biomarkers involved in oncogenesis. This study aims to compare EV concentration and molecular content in RA patients treated with different targeted therapies. The objective is to identify treatment-related differences in EV profiles that may contribute to lung cancer development and improve risk stratification.
primary_outcomes: Plasma extracellular vesicle (EV) concentration at inclusion
title: The Impact of Rheumatoid Arthritis Treatments on the Modulation of Extracellular Vesicles and Other Biomarkers Involved in the Development of Lung Cancer

brief_summary:
Chronic subdural hematoma is a collection of old blood on the surface of the brain that mainly affects older adults. It is often treated by draining the blood through a small hole in the skull (burr hole), under local anesthesia combined with intravenous sedation while the patient keeps breathing spontaneously. Propofol and dexmedetomidine are the two sedatives most commonly used for this purpose.

This randomized pilot study will compare how well each drug maintains a moderate and stable level of sedation during surgery. Sixty adults will be randomly assigned to receive either propofol by target-controlled infusion or dexmedetomidine. The main outcome is the percentage of surgical time spent at the target sedation level, defined as a Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale (RASS) score between -2 and -3.

The study will also compare the time needed to reach the target sedation, breathing and cardiovascular side effects, sedation failures, recovery time, and surgeon and anesthesiologist satisfaction. The results will be used to estimate the sample size of a future confirmatory trial.
primary_outcomes: Percentage of time within target sedation
title: Propofol Target-Controlled Infusion Versus Dexmedetomidine for Sedation During Chronic Subdural Hematoma Surgery Under Local Anesthesia

brief_summary: This randomized clinical trial aims to compare regenerative endodontic treatment using injectable platelet-rich fibrin (i-PRF) with conventional root canal treatment in mature necrotic anterior teeth with chronic apical periodontitis. Clinical and radiographic healing, inflammatory biomarkers in gingival crevicular fluid (IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α), postoperative pain, analgesic intake, and pulp vitality recovery will be evaluated over a 6-month follow-up. brief_summary: The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate the efficacy of a 5-day short-course external trigeminal nerve stimulation (eTNS) regimen in patients with acute ischemic stroke. The main questions it aims to answer are whether a 5-day eTNS intervention can significantly improve the neurological response rate at Day 30 compared to sham stimulation, and whether this short-course treatment yields sustained improvements in neuropsychiatric symptoms (depression, anxiety, and insomnia) over a 90-day follow-up period. Researchers will compare the active eTNS group to a sham-controlled group to see if the 5-day stimulation provides a sustained neuroprotective effect. Participants will be randomly assigned (1:1) to receive either active eTNS or sham eTNS for 5 consecutive nights within 72 hours of stroke onset, in addition to standard medical therapy, and will undergo neurological and functional assessments (NIHSS, mRS, BI) at baseline (Day 0), Day 5, Day 30, Day 60, and Day 90, as well as complete neuropsychiatric questionnaires (PHQ-9, GAD-7, and ISI) during the follow-up visits to evaluate their mood and sleep quality. In addition, brain imaging data and blood samples will be collected at baseline (Day 0) and after the 5-day intervention (Day 5) for exploratory analyses of infarct volume and peripheral inflammatory markers.
title: Short-Term External Trigeminal Nerve Stimulation for Acute Ischemic Stroke: A Sham-Controlled Trial

brief_summary:
Episiotomy is a surgical incision made in the perineum during the second stage of labor. The suturing (repair) process following episiotomy causes significant acute perineal pain and state anxiety in women due to the rich nerve supply of the perineum. Although the physiological and psychological benefits of early skin-to-skin contact (SSC) for mothers and newborns are widely reported in the literature, studies evaluating the effects of SSC on maternal pain and anxiety during episiotomy repair, when surgical stress is intense, are limited.

The aim of this study is to investigate the effects of early skin-to-skin contact during episiotomy repair on women's pain and state anxiety levels and to compare the group receiving SSC with the group receiving standard routine care. The study will be conducted as a randomized controlled experimental study, and the sample size has been calculated using power analysis. The data collection tools will include the Descriptive Information Form, Visual Analog Scale (VAS), and Spielberger State Anxiety Inventory.

SSC applied during repair stimulates endogenous oxytocin release, reduces hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis and sympathetic nervous system activity, supports the parasympathetic system, and provides natural analgesic and anxiolytic effects. It also shifts the mother's attention from the pain of the surgical procedure to her baby. Conducted within the framework of woman-centered midwifery care, this study aims to address the gap in the literature regarding the analgesic and anxiolytic effects of SSC during episiotomy repair and to contribute evidence-based knowledge to clinical midwifery practice.
title: THE EFFECT OF SKIN-TO-SKIN CONTACT ON PAIN AND ANXIETY DURING EPISIOTOMY REPAIR

brief_summary:
Non-specific neck pain is neck pain that cannot be attributed to any known, specific pathology such as inflammatory disease, cancer, fracture or infection. Non-specific neck pain accounts for a large proportion of musculoskeletal disorders among young people, especially university students, due to prolonged static postures, prolonged screen time and poor ergonomic habits. In some cases, muscular imbalances or excessive activity of the cervical and periscapular muscles due to prolonged forward head posture is suggested to be the cause. In other cases, altered neuromuscular function, limited movement of the scapulothoracic region resulting in altered cervical mechanics or mild dysfunction of the facet joints between cervical vertebrae may be the cause. In addition to these, there may be other minor disorders that cause pain and impairment of function in the connective tissues and surrounding soft tissue components in the neck and upper thorax. When symptoms last longer than three months, the term "chronic" non-specific neck pain is used.

Non-specific neck pain has been treated with numerous therapeutic interventions such as manual therapy, exercise based approaches, dry needling, postural correction and soft tissue procedures. Muscle Energy Technique (MET) is an active osteopathic manual therapies method that uses the patient's own contractions to lengthen and relax hypertonic muscles and improve joint mobility. The purpose of this study is to compare the effects of Muscle Energy Technique with and without Scapulothoracic Mobilization on pain, range of motion and disability among university students with non-specific neck pain. The study design will be a randomized clinical trial and evaluation will be done using Numeric Pain Rating Scale (NPRS), Neck Disability Index (NDI) and Goniometer. However, the most effective combination of these interventions as a method of rehabilitation for altered cervical kinematics and pain. Further research is necessary to determine the best effective mix of these interventions as a rehabilitation strategy for non-specific neck pain in college students, which reflects the complexity of the condition. This study aims to assess the response of university students with non-specific neck pain to Muscle Energy Technique with and without Scapulothoracic Mobilization in terms of pain, range of motion and impairment. A randomized clinical trial will be used as the study design. The Neck Disability Index (NDI), Goniometer and Numeric Pain Rating Scale (NPRS) will be used for evaluation. The subjects will be divided into two groups at random using non-probability convenient sampling; Group A will receive Muscle Energy Technique in addition to Scapulothoracic Mobilizations, while Group B will receive Muscle Energy Technique alone. Prior to the application of the technique, both groups will receive a 15-minute moist heat as a basic treatment for non-specific neck pain; both groups will receive 12 sessions over the course of four weeks; measurements of all outcome variables will be taken at baseline, the second week, and the fourth week. The results will be analyzed using SPSS 24.
lead_sponsor: University of Management and Technology Lahore
title: Effects of Muscle Energy Technique With and Without Scapulothoracic Mobilization on Neck Pain in Students

brief_summary:
Background. Childhood anemia affects more than 40% of under-five children in Ethiopia, where iron supplementation has achieved limited success and locally grounded, sustainable strategies are needed. Red teff (Eragrostis tef) is an iron-rich, gluten-free staple crop. We evaluated whether a red teff porridge improves hemoglobin in anemic infants and toddlers, and quantified its cost and potential environmental impact relative to animal-source iron-rich foods.

Methods. In a self-controlled pre-post feeding trial in East Gojjam Zone, Ethiopia, anemic children received 42 g home-prepared red teff porridge providing about 77 mg iron per day for 60 days. The primary outcome, the change in hemoglobin, was analyzed with covariate-adjusted models (n = 32 after excluding one implausible value), with covariates selected on biological grounds and additionally screened by cross-validated LASSO. The cost and greenhouse-gas emissions (GHGE) of red teff were compared with beef, lamb and egg per milligram of absorbed iron and per gram of protein, with substitution and sensitivity analyses.
title: Triple Outcome Evaluation of Red Teff Intervention for Infant Anemia, Environmental Health, and Economic Feasibility in Ethiopia: A Self-controlled Pre-post Study

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical study is to evaluate changes in the appearance of horizontal neck lines after treatment with DOT PN (Rejuran S), a polynucleotide-based injectable medical device, administered using a dual-plane injection technique in adults aged 25 to 65 years with mild to moderate horizontal neck lines.

The main question it aims to answer is:

\- What is the mean change in horizontal neck wrinkle depth from the start of the study (Week 0) to Week 16, as measured by 3D imaging?

* Attend 7 study visits over 24 weeks for 3D imaging, wrinkle grading, questionnaires, and safety checks

The injection technique, including the use of a blunt-tip cannula for the deeper layer, is a study-specific procedure defined by the study protocol and standardized across all study sites.
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in Horizontal Neck Wrinkle Depth at Week 16

brief_summary: This randomized controlled study aimed to evaluate the effect of temporary tattoo application on women's perception of body exposure during sexual activity and body satisfaction. brief_summary:
Obstructive sleep apnea causes repeated pauses in breathing during sleep. Breathing efforts against an occluded airway may change how blood flows through the heart and how blood drains from the brain.

This study will examine these changes in 25 adults with severe obstructive sleep apnea and 25 adults without sleep apnea, aged 18 to 65 years. Participants will attend a screening visit and one magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) visit. MRI will measure blood flow in major vessels in the chest, neck and brain at rest and during brief, standardized breathing maneuvers. Participants with sleep apnea will also be studied during obstructive apneas while sleeping in the scanner, and during continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP), which keeps the airway open.

The main objective is to quantify changes in blood flow rate and peak blood velocity before, during and at the end of obstructive apneas. The study will also compare responses to breathing maneuvers and resting blood flow between groups, and assess changes associated with CPAP in participants with sleep apnea. Secondary brain MRI outcomes are total perivascular space burden, burden in the basal ganglia and centrum semiovale, and the DTI ALPS index. BrainAGE, the difference between estimated brain age and chronological age in years, is an exploratory outcome. These MRI markers are compared between groups at baseline and after CPAP treatment.
primary_outcomes: Change in volumetric blood flow rate during spontaneous obstructive apneas
Change in peak blood velocity during spontaneous obstructive apneas
title: Heart and Brain Blood Flow in Obstructive Sleep Apnea

brief_summary:
This study aims to compare two injectable materials, calcium hydroxylapatite (Radiesse®) and hyaluronic acid, for treating gaps between the teeth caused by loss of gum tissue. These gaps, commonly known as "black triangles," can affect the appearance of a person's smile and may cause food to become trapped between the teeth.

Hyaluronic acid has been used to improve the appearance of these gaps, but its effects may not last for a long time. Calcium hydroxylapatite is another injectable material that may help the body produce collagen, a natural protein that supports gum tissue. This study will investigate whether calcium hydroxylapatite can provide better or longer-lasting results compared with hyaluronic acid.

The study will take place at the Faculty of Dentistry, King Abdulaziz University, Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. Approximately 20 healthy adults who have two similar gaps between their front teeth will be invited to participate.

Each participant will receive both treatments. One gap will be treated with diluted calcium hydroxylapatite, while the other will be treated with hyaluronic acid. The treatment for each site will be selected randomly to ensure a fair comparison. Each site will receive one injection.

Participants will be examined before treatment and again after 3 weeks, 3 months, and 6 months to assess the results.

During these visits, photographs and clinical measurements will be taken to evaluate changes in the size of the gaps and the amount of gum tissue between the teeth. Participants will also be asked about their satisfaction with the appearance of their gums, any discomfort experienced during treatment, and whether they have noticed an improvement in their smile. Any side effects or complications will also be recorded.

The researchers will compare how well the two materials improve the appearance of the gaps and how long the improvements last.

Participation will be voluntary, and all participants will receive information about the study before signing a consent form. Their personal information will be kept confidential, and they may withdraw from the study at any time without affecting their dental care.

The main goal of this study is to identify whether diluted calcium hydroxylapatite or hyaluronic acid provides better and longer-lasting improvement in the appearance of gaps between the teeth. The findings may help dentists choose more effective, minimally invasive treatments for patients with missing gum tissue between their teeth.
title: Comparing Calcium Hydroxylapatite and Hyaluronic Acid for Interdental Papilla Reconstruction

brief_summary: The NEPHRON study is a prospective, randomized controlled trial evaluating the use of an automated fluid management system during kidney transplantation. A total of 48 adult patients will be randomly assigned to either an Assisted Fluid Management (AFM) group or a standard care group. The primary objective is to compare the total volume of intravenous fluids administered during surgery. Secondary outcomes include intraoperative hypotension, vasopressor requirements, postoperative kidney function, and complications. The study aims to assess whether AFM-guided therapy can optimize intraoperative fluid administration in kidney transplant recipients.

brief_summary: This single-center, dual-cohort, exploratory phase II trial evaluates the efficacy and safety of trastuzumab rezetecan (SHR-A1811), an anti-HER2 antibody-drug conjugate (ADC), with or without the anti-PD-L1 antibody adebrelimab as neoadjuvant therapy in patients with locally advanced, resectable esophageal, gastric, or gastroesophageal junction (GEJ) adenocarcinoma. Approximately 62 patients aged ≥18 years with pathologically confirmed resectable disease (cT1b-2N+M0 or cT3-4NanyM0, American Joint Committee on Cancer \[AJCC\] 8th edition), HER2 intermediate-to-high expression (immunohistochemistry \[IHC\] 2+ or 3+), no prior systemic antitumor therapy for esophageal or gastric adenocarcinoma, and Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status 0-1 are planned for enrollment. Eligible participants will be randomly assigned to receive either trastuzumab rezetecan monotherapy or trastuzumab rezetecan plus adebrelimab for 3 cycles (each cycle 21 days), followed by radical surgery. The primary endpoint is pathological complete response (pCR). Secondary endpoints include major pathological response (MPR), R0 resection rate, objective response rate (ORR), event-free survival (EFS), overall survival (OS), and safety. Exploratory objectives include biomarker analysis to identify predictors of response to HER2 ADC therapy with or without PD-L1 blockade.
title: Neoadjuvant SHR-A1811 ± Adebrelimab in GC/GEJ

brief_summary:
Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) is a type of air pollution made up of extremely tiny particles that can harm our health. Because PM2.5 particles are so small, they can travel deep into the lungs when we breathe. Exposure to PM2.5 can worsen asthma, cause breathing problems, increase the risk of heart attacks, and lead to early death, especially for people with existing heart or lung conditions. In California's Bayview Hunters Point (BVHP), a San Francisco community already facing high levels of air pollution and health impacts, sources of PM2.5 include industrial activity, commuter traffic, heavy-duty diesel trucks, freight trains, and port and maritime activities.

The Reducing Exposure with Air Cleaners and Technology (REACT) Study is a partnership between UC Berkeley, UC San Francisco, and Brightline Defense. The goal is to see if air cleaners (also called air purifiers) can help reduce indoor PM2.5 levels and improve respiratory health.

For this study, we'll be recruiting 100 households in BVHP to participate. In each home, we'll monitor indoor PM2.5 levels and the health status of household members who are 13 years old or older and have asthma or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Each home will be part of the study for 90 to 120 days, depending on scheduling. Households must reside in BVHP for the duration of the study and not have used an air cleaner in their home within the last 6 months.

On Day 1, each household will receive a PurpleAir indoor air quality monitor to measure PM2.5 levels in their home.

* For the first 30 days, we'll measure the home's normal air quality (baseline).
* After 30 days, each household will receive an air cleaner (Figure 2) with information about how to best use it.
* At that point, we'll also turn on a PM2.5 indicator light on half of the PurpleAir monitors. For the other half, we'll keep that indicator light turned off. This helps us study whether seeing the air quality in real time changes how people use the air cleaner.
* For the next 30 days, we'll continue monitoring indoor PM2.5 levels. We'll also track how often the air cleaner is used with smart plug data loggers.
* After 60 days, if a household isn't using the air cleaner much or it doesn't seem to be working well, we'll offer more training and support.
* We'll continue monitoring over the final 30 days of the study.
interventions: PM2.5 Monitor with Visual Air Quality Indicator
primary_outcomes: Air Quality: Absolute Change in Daily Average Indoor Fine Particulate Matter (PM2.5) Concentration
Air Quality: Percent Change in Daily Average Indoor Fine Particulate Matter (PM2.5) Concentration
Difference in Self-Reported Respiratory Symptoms using Breathlessness, Cough, and Sputum Scale (BCSS) or Asthma Control Test (ACT)
title: Reducing Exposure With Air Cleaners and Technology

brief_summary:
PRECISION-E2 is a Phase IIa randomized, placebo-controlled study evaluating the pharmacodynamic profile, safety and tolerability of teverelix in premenopausal women with moderate-to-severe pain associated with endometriosis in the United Arab Emirates. The study will characterize the magnitude and duration of estradiol suppression following a single administration of teverelix and evaluate dose and route of administration, including subcutaneous and intramuscular administration, to inform subsequent clinical development.

The study also incorporates a prospective precision medicine component designed to explore associations between genomic variation and pharmacodynamic and clinical response to teverelix. In participants enrolled in the Emirati Genome Program, genomic data will be integrated with hormonal, pharmacokinetic and clinical outcomes to investigate potential biological determinants of treatment response.
primary_outcomes: Percentage of Participants With Serum Estradiol Maintained Within 20-50 pg/mL for at Least 14 Consecutive Days

brief_summary:
Virtual Reality (VR) is becoming an increasingly important tool in mental healthcare, offering new ways to enhance patient treatment. Over the past decade, there's been growing interest in using VR therapies because they create immersive, controlled environments tailored to individual therapeutic needs. In a safe and controlled, therapeutic setting, these environments can help patients work through difficult emotions and experiences. However, despite its potential, the widespread adoption of VR in routine mental healthcare has been slow due to the high costs of the necessary technology, making it less accessible for many patients and therapists.

VR is particularly valuable in mental health therapy because it can evoke strong cognitive, emotional, and physical responses, much like traditional therapeutic techniques that use imagery or visualisation. Research has shown that VR can offer unique benefits, such as real-time monitoring of a patient's responses and creating customised exposure therapies that safely mimic real-world scenarios. These features can be incredibly effective in treating conditions like Post Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD), anxiety, and phobias.

This study aims to overcome the barriers to VR adoption by developing a more affordable approach to creating virtual environments that can be used in everyday mental healthcare. Collaborating with a software company called ProPeer Solutions, the project has created a process called "VR Photoscan." This method allows for the creation of virtual environments at a lower cost, making it more accessible to clinics and therapists. The ultimate goal is to integrate VR into standard mental health treatments, making this innovative technology available to more people who could benefit from it, specifically within routine psychological therapy services for adults with PTSD.
title: Virtual Reality Assisted Trauma Focused CBT

brief_summary:
This multicenter, prospective, pilot randomized controlled trial aims to evaluate the feasibility and preliminary efficacy of a 16-week structured exercise program (SEP) in patients with hematologic malignancies, including acute myeloid leukemia, lymphoma, and multiple myeloma.

A total of 75 patients will be randomized in a 1:1 ratio to either a supervised exercise intervention or a control group receiving usual care and general advice on physical activity.

The intervention consists of a personalized, hybrid exercise program combining supervised home- and gym-based training, aerobic and resistance exercises, balance and stretching activities, and behavioral counseling.

The primary objective is to assess the feasibility of the intervention in terms of adherence to the exercise program and patient satisfaction.

Secondary objectives include evaluating intervention-related adverse events, patient-reported burden, health-related quality of life, fatigue, physical fitness, anthropometric parameters, and physical activity levels.

Assessments will be conducted at baseline, approximately 8 weeks, 16 weeks (end of intervention), and 24 weeks after randomization.
primary_outcomes: Adherence to the Structured Exercise Program
Patient Satisfaction With the Structured Exercise Program
title: The Value of a Tailored-based, Exercise Program for Improving Quality of Life of Patients With Hematologic Malignancies: a Pilot Randomized Trial

brief_summary: Some patients with gastric cancer have enlarged para-aortic lymph nodes, also called No. 16 lymph nodes, at diagnosis. After standard chemoimmunotherapy, these lymph nodes may shrink to less than 10 mm on imaging, but it is uncertain whether microscopic cancer remains and whether surgically removing these nodes improves disease control. This single-center randomized exploratory trial will enroll 32 patients whose suspicious No. 16a2 and/or No. 16b1 lymph nodes have regressed to less than 10 mm after 2 to 8 cycles of standard chemoimmunotherapy and who have no disease progression or new distant metastases. Participants will be assigned 1:1 to curative-intent gastrectomy with standard D2 lymphadenectomy either with or without para-aortic lymph node dissection. The main outcome is progression-free survival at 2 years after randomization.
interventions: Gastrectomy with D2 lymphadenectomy plus para-aortic lymph node dissection

brief_summary:
Every year, a lot of older people fall. These falls often lead to serious injuries and are a common reason for moving into care homes, increasing the amount of paid support at home or needing to rely more on family, friends and neighbours for informal support. Falling can make people lose confidence in their abilities to do different activities, leading to loneliness and physical weakness, increasing the risk of more falls. It's important to identify why someone might fall and put things in place to try and reduce these risks. This needs to be done whilst also supporting people to be confident and continue to do the things they enjoy doing.

Action Falls is an intervention that aims to find out why someone might fall and suggests ways to help, like checking their medication and encouraging them to stay active. It was first created to try and prevent falls in care homes. We have now adapted the intervention for older people living in their own homes that are supporting by home care services. We now need to try out the adapted intervention to see what people think about it and explore whether it can help manage falls and independence.

The Action Falls for home care intervention includes:

* Training for home care and reablement staff
* Information and resources to help identify potential risks and suggest potential actions
* Information for older people and families to consider potential falls risks and actions In order to evaluate the Action Falls for home care we are undertaking a study over 2 years where the intervention will be delivered across home care organisations in Nottinghamshire and Lincolnshire. We are asking home care staff and older people to take part in different parts of the research to explore the different views on how well the intervention has been delivered and whether it has improved confidence in managing falls and promoted independence and activity for older people.
title: Implementing Action Falls for Domiciliary Care

brief_summary:
This study evaluated whether video-based education before surgery could reduce anxiety and improve early recovery in patients undergoing anal fistula surgery under spinal anesthesia.

A total of 72 adult patients participated in this randomized controlled trial. Participants were randomly assigned to one of two groups. The intervention group received standard preoperative information and watched an approximately 8-minute educational video explaining spinal anesthesia, the surgical procedure, pain management, and early postoperative recovery. The control group received standard verbal and written information only.

The main objective was to determine whether video-based education reduced anxiety immediately before surgery, measured using the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI-S).

The study also evaluated other outcomes, including anxiety measured using another questionnaire (APAIS), postoperative pain, pain medication requirements, and patients' willingness to undergo spinal anesthesia again.

The study aimed to investigate whether adding a short educational video to routine preoperative counseling could improve patients' psychological preparation and early perioperative experience.
primary_outcomes: Preoperative Anxiety Measured by the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI-S)
title: Video-Based Preoperative Education for Anxiety in Patients Undergoing Anal Fistula Surgery

brief_summary:
This randomized controlled trial will investigate the effects of different aquatic power training dosing strategies and creatine supplementation on functional and multisystem adaptations in community-dwelling older adults.

Participants will be randomly allocated to one of five parallel groups: (1) aquatic power training regulated according to rating of perceived exertion during the first repetition (RPE-1) plus placebo; (2) aquatic power training using a conventional time-based dosing strategy plus placebo; (3) time-based aquatic power training plus creatine supplementation; (4) sedentary control plus placebo; or (5) sedentary control plus creatine supplementation.

The intervention will last 16 weeks. Aquatic training will be performed three times per week for approximately 60 minutes per session. Participants allocated to creatine supplementation will receive 3 g/day of creatine monohydrate, whereas the corresponding placebo groups will receive a visually indistinguishable placebo following the same supplementation schedule.

The primary outcomes will assess body composition, muscle strength, and functional capacity. Additional outcomes will examine bone health, cardiometabolic health, inflammatory and oxidative stress biomarkers, immune function, neurobiological and cognitive function, quality of life, sleep quality, psychological status, fatigue, and affective state.

Assessments will be performed before and after the 16-week intervention.
primary_outcomes: Change in Body Composition via Dual-Energy X-ray Absorptiometry (DXA)
Change in lower limb Isokinetic muscle strength
Change in upper limb Isokinetic muscle Strength
Change in functional mobility and agility performance
Change in lower body functional performance
title: Aquatic Power Training Dosing Strategies and Creatine Supplementation in Older Adults

brief_summary: This study aims to evaluate the feasibility and preliminary biocompatibility of a novel lactoferrin-based ventilation tube and its manufacturing process for use in implantable medical materials. Patients with otitis media with effusion who are scheduled to undergo tympanostomy tube placement will be enrolled. Before insertion of the standard ventilation tube, the novel lactoferrin-based tube will be temporarily placed at the tympanic membrane incision site. Its handling characteristics and preliminary material properties will be assessed, including successful placement, mechanical strength, and structural integrity during manipulation. Local reactions of the tympanic membrane and surrounding tissues following brief contact will also be observed. The findings will provide preliminary evidence to support further material optimization and subsequent studies. This study is not intended to evaluate the long-term clinical efficacy or safety of the tube as an indwelling tympanostomy device.

brief_summary: This study compares two airway devices used during general anesthesia in children: a second-generation laryngeal mask (SafeLM LMA) and a third-generation video laryngeal mask (SafeLM Video LMA). Both devices are CE-marked and routinely used in clinical practice. The study will include 90 children aged 2 to 8 years who are scheduled for elective surgery. Children will be randomly assigned to one of two groups (45 per group), and one of the two devices will be placed after anesthesia induction. The main outcome is oropharyngeal leak pressure, which shows how well the mask seals the airway. Other outcomes include success at the first insertion attempt, number of attempts, view of the vocal cords (video group), heart rate and blood pressure changes, and complications such as laryngospasm, low oxygen levels, sore throat, hoarseness, and nausea/vomiting. The study aims to show whether video-guided placement improves airway seal and safety in children.

brief_summary:
Patients with severe acquired brain injury (sABI) and disorders of consciousness (DoC) require intensive interdisciplinary rehabilitation involving healthcare professionals, patients, and family caregivers. Caregivers play a key role in supporting patients and ensuring continuity of care, yet they frequently experience high levels of psychological distress, anxiety, depression, caregiver burden, and reduced quality of life. Previous studies have highlighted the need for clearer communication and greater caregiver involvement throughout the rehabilitation process.

The Social and Family Evaluation (SAFE) scale was developed to actively involve caregivers in monitoring patients with DoC. Derived from the Coma Recovery Scale-Revised (CRS-R), SAFE is a simplified, caregiver-friendly observational tool that enables family members to report clinically relevant behaviors observed during daily interactions. Preliminary validation demonstrated excellent psychometric properties, including high internal consistency, excellent test-retest reliability, and good criterion validity compared with the CRS-R. However, its effectiveness has not yet been investigated in the subacute rehabilitation setting.

The primary aim of this study is to evaluate whether the use of the SAFE scale improves caregivers' illness perceptions. Secondary objectives are to assess its impact on caregiver satisfaction with rehabilitation, decisional conflict, anxiety, depression, prolonged grief, and caregiver burden.

This is a non-profit, prospective, multicenter, single-blind randomized controlled trial involving 68 caregiver-patient dyads recruited from three intensive neurorehabilitation units of the Don Carlo Gnocchi Foundation in Florence, Milan, and Sant'Angelo dei Lombardi (Italy). Adult caregivers of patients with DoC admitted within three months after brain injury will be randomly assigned (1:1) to either the SAFE intervention group or a standard-care control group. Randomization will be stratified according to caregiver relationship (parent vs. non-parent) and patient diagnosis (vegetative state/unresponsive wakefulness syndrome vs. other DoC).

At baseline (T0), caregivers will complete the Brief Illness Perception Questionnaire (BIPQ), Family Strain Questionnaire (FSQ), Prolonged Grief Disorder-12 (PG-12), Beck Depression Inventory-II (BDI-II), and State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI-Y). Patients will be assessed using the Coma Recovery Scale-Revised (CRS-R) and the Level of Cognitive Functioning (LCF).

Caregivers allocated to the SAFE group will receive standardized training on the SAFE scale and complete it at 2 weeks (T1) and 6 weeks (T2), together with repeated BIPQ assessments. Control participants will receive routine clinical care and complete the BIPQ only. Both groups will receive the same psychoeducational booklet as standard care.

At the final follow-up (T3, 10 weeks after enrollment), caregivers will repeat all baseline assessments and additionally complete the Family Satisfaction in Intensive Care Unit (FS-ICU) and the Decisional Conflict Scale (DCS). Patients will undergo repeat CRS-R and LCF assessments together with the Glasgow Outcome Scale-Extended (GOSE).

The primary endpoint is the BIPQ Illness Coherence score at T2. The primary analysis will use ANCOVA adjusted for baseline values. Based on preliminary data, 68 caregivers will be enrolled to detect a clinically meaningful difference between groups while accounting for an expected 20% dropout rate. A blinded sample-size re-estimation will be performed after recruitment of the first 30 participants.

Secondary analyses will evaluate the effects of the SAFE intervention on caregiver burden, prolonged grief, anxiety, depression, family satisfaction, and decisional conflict using adjusted statistical models.

The study is considered low risk, as all procedures are consistent with routine clinical practice. If effective, the SAFE scale may enhance caregiver understanding of the patient's condition, improve communication with the rehabilitation team, promote shared decision-making, reduce psychological distress, and support a more family-centered approach to neurorehabilitation.
conditions: Caregiver Satisfaction and Connectedness to Clinic
Disorders of Consciousness Due to Severe Brain Injury
interventions: Caregiver training and administration of SAFE scale
primary_outcomes: Caregivers' Perceived Understanding of Their Relative's Clinical Condition
title: Comprehensive Assessment of Rehabilitation Experience Using the SAFE Scale

brief_summary: This study is a national, fully virtual Type 3 hybrid implementation-effectiveness clinical trial using the Multiphase Optimization Strategy (MOST) to evaluate implementation strategies designed to optimize delivery of the Healthy Choices (HC) behavioral intervention through the HealthMpowerment (HMP) digital health platform. A total of 360 emerging adults ages 18-29 who are eligible for antiretroviral therapy (ART) or pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) and report recent alcohol use will be randomized using a factorial design to combinations of three implementation strategies: a personalized video introduction to an HC peer counselor, tailored digital messaging, and asynchronous support from an HC counselor. All participants receive HC-HMP. The primary implementation outcome is HC direct-to-consumer fidelity, measured by the number of HC counseling sessions completed. Secondary outcomes include HMP fidelity assessed using platform-generated paradata, alcohol use, and HIV transmission risk. Participants complete assessments at baseline, 3 months, and 6 months.
title: HC-HMP: Healthy Choices Implementation Trial

brief_summary: Advanced heart failure, affecting 7 million Americans, has multiple causes and results in greatly increased risk of disability and death. A major problem is sudden cardiac death, when the damaged heart develops an abnormal pattern of electrical conduction that can result in cessation of heart activity. While placement of an Implantable Cardioverter-Defibrillator (ICD) in a patient's chest can help prevent sudden cardiac death, these devices have several important downsides. This protocol focuses on development of a digital decision aid that helps heart failure patients make informed decisions that balance the benefits and downsides of ICD placement. This protocol covers the use of participant surveys, focus groups, and interviews to obtain the needed background information to guide the development of this digital tool, which will be subsequently tested against usual care in a randomized clinical trial. The study design is best described as a mixed methods evaluation and refinement of a digital app to improve ICD decision-making. In the future, the present protocol will be modified to create a new protocol that covers the needed human subjects requirements for performance of this clinical trial.
interventions: Arm A: Online, patient-facing decision-making aid (app) with personalized risk information.
Arm B - Online, patient-facing decision-making app without personalized risk information.
title: Evaluating a Digital Aid to Improve ICD Decisions

brief_summary: Emergence delirium (ED) is a frequent complication in children undergoing general anesthesia, particularly following ENT procedures such as adenotonsillectomy. brief_summary: Fibromyalgia is a condition that may lead to a decline in respiratory function, as well as impaired oxygen delivery to and utilization by the muscles-factors that contribute to fatigue and reduced exercise capacity. However, this aspect remains insufficiently studied and is not yet clearly understood. In this context, this study aims to compare upper extremity functional exercise capacity, respiratory and peripheral muscle strength, muscle oxygenation, pain, and quality of life in patients with fibromyalgia syndrome against those of healthy individuals.
title: Respiratory Function in Fibromiyalgia Syndrome

brief_summary: This study is being done to better understand how the immune system responds to vaccination against influenza and rabies. Researchers want to study how immune responses develop and change over time in the blood and in the lymph nodes that drain the vaccination site, following vaccination with two vaccines licensed by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA): the seasonal trivalent influenza vaccine (TIV) and the rabies vaccine (RabAvert). By studying these samples, researchers hope to learn how the body produces high-quality, long-lasting antibody and memory immune responses after vaccination. The study will also compare immune responses in younger adults to immune responses in older adults, because prior research suggests that the immune system's ability to respond to vaccination weakens with age.
primary_outcomes: Rabies-specific antibody titers at day 29 compared to pre-vaccination baseline.
title: Age-Associated Differences in Germinal Center Responses to Influenza and Rabies Vaccination in Humans

brief_summary:
This retrospective multicohort observational study evaluates whether the PaO2/FiO2 ratio (P/F ratio) organizes heterogeneity in the association between early systemic corticosteroid exposure and mortality among critically ill patients with sepsis.

The study uses one internal critical-care cohort (ICCA) and two external critical-care databases (MIMIC and eICU). Analyses include internal discovery, broad external testing, reconstruction of external cohorts toward vasopressor-anchored shock-decision contexts, realized-exposure observational analyses, and strategy-level analyses using a simplified clone-censor-weighting framework (Lite-CCW).

The primary objective is to characterize whether corticosteroid-associated outcome patterns differ across P/F strata and whether similar directional patterns are observed across independent ICU datasets after decision-context reconstruction. The study is hypothesis-generating and does not assign corticosteroid treatment or define a clinical treatment-selection rule.
title: PF-Organized Corticosteroid-Associated Heterogeneity in Sepsis

brief_summary:
Juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) is the most common chronic rheumatic disease in children, causing persistent joint inflammation, pain, and functional impairment. Current monitoring relies on clinical scores, laboratory markers, and imaging, which are often resource intensive. Infrared thermography (IRT) is a non-invasive, radiation-free method that detects skin temperature changes potentially reflecting joint inflammation. Evidence in pediatric populations is limited, but IRT could provide an objective, reproducible, and child-friendly tool. This study aims to evaluate IRT's diagnostic accuracy by comparing it with clinical scores, laboratory markers, and ultrasound Doppler, to assess its utility as a complementary monitoring tool.

Patients with JIA will undergo clinical examination, routine blood tests, and IRT at baseline, 1 month, and 3 months. Control patients will participate in a single IRT session and, a CRP/ESR/blood test; if a biological workup is already planned as part of their routine care, existing results will be collected, and no additional sampling will be performed. IRT will follow a standardized protocol, including an acclimatization period, predefined positioning, and acquisition of three consecutive images per joint. After completion of the study, JIA patients will resume their standard-of-care follow-up.
interventions: single IRT session and a minimal blood test
primary_outcomes: variation of IRT measure between both groups

variation of IRT measure between both groups
title: The Use of Infrared Cameras for Detecting Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis

brief_summary:
This prospective, single-center mechanistic pilot study will investigate the electrophysiological dose-response to anterior thalamic deep brain stimulation (ANT-DBS) in 10 adults with drug-resistant focal epilepsy undergoing clinically indicated DBS implantation.

Using local field potentials (LFPs) recorded from implanted sensing-enabled DBS leads, investigators will assess stimulation-induced changes in slow-gamma (20-50 Hz) power. Standardized acute stimulation challenges will be performed at DBS activation (2.0 mA), 1 month after activation (2.0 and 3.5 mA), and 3 months after activation (2.0, 3.5, and up to 5.0 mA, as tolerated). Each amplitude will be tested at least twice against a stimulation-OFF baseline.

The primary objective is to characterize the amplitude-dependent electrophysiological response, with the hypothesis that higher stimulation amplitudes produce greater slow-gamma suppression. Secondary objectives include assessing response reproducibility, characterizing longitudinal LFP adaptation during the first 3 months, investigating associations with electrode location and modeled electric fields, and exploring relationships with seizure-frequency reduction during months 7-12 after stimulation activation.
interventions: Anterior thalamic deep brain stimulation with a standardized amplitude schedule and acute stimulation challenges
primary_outcomes: Stimulation-Induced Change in Anterior Thalamic Slow-Gamma (20-50 Hz) Power at 2.0, 3.5 and 5.0 mA
title: Electrophysiological Dose-Response to Anterior Thalamic Deep Brain Stimulation in Drug-Resistant Focal Epilepsy

brief_summary: Total knee arthroplasty (TKA) remains the definitive treatment for advanced knee osteoarthritis and continues to be performed with increasing frequency worldwide. However, patient dissatisfaction remains reported in up to one-fifth of cases, despite technically successful procedures and acceptable radiographic results. This discrepancy has shifted attention toward early functional recovery and patient-reported outcomes as more meaningful indicators of success. In response, technological innovations such as robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty have been introduced to enhance surgical precision and reduce alignment outliers. This study aims to determine whether these technical advantages translate into improved early clinical outcomes by comparing patient satisfaction, functional results, radiological accuracy, and perioperative parameters between robotic-assisted and conventional total knee arthroplasty over one year.

brief_summary:
This prospective clinical study will evaluate the feasibility, performance, and safety of the LambdaGuide System for obtaining point-to-point measurements of observable genitourinary anatomy during cystoscopic procedures in adult men. The system is intended to provide measurements of anatomical structures visible during cystoscopy without influencing clinical diagnosis or treatment decisions.

The study will assess successful calibration, spatial capture, measurement point selection, and completion of point-to-point measurements. Device usability, procedural workflow effects, and adverse events will also be evaluated. Optional comparisons with known-dimension references may be performed for descriptive purposes.

LambdaGuide measurements will not be used to guide or modify clinical care.
title: Observational Study of the LambdaGuide System for Measurement of Observable Genitourinary Anatomy During Cystoscopic Procedures in Men

brief_summary: Ankle injuries are a common reason for emergency department visits. Although fractures are relatively uncommon, ankle and foot X-rays are frequently ordered to exclude them. The Ottawa Ankle Rules are clinical decision rules designed to help healthcare professionals identify patients who require radiographic imaging. This study evaluated whether an electronic pop-up reminder of the Ottawa Ankle Rules could reduce the number of ankle and foot X-rays prescribed in the emergency department. The study also assessed adherence to the Ottawa Ankle Rules and evaluated their diagnostic performance for identifying fractures.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of Patients Receiving Ankle or Foot Radiography

brief_summary:
This study will compare two balloon inflation strategies during transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), a procedure used to replace a severely narrowed aortic valve through a catheter. A balloon-expandable replacement valve may not fully expand during its initial placement. An additional inflation using the same balloon and the same inflation volume, called "Double-Tap," may improve valve expansion and function. Its benefits and risks need to be evaluated in a randomized trial.

This prospective, multicenter study aims to include 250 adults with symptomatic severe aortic stenosis undergoing TAVI with an Edwards SAPIEN-family balloon-expandable valve. After successful valve implantation, participants for whom an additional inflation is considered technically feasible and clinically appropriate will be randomly assigned in equal numbers to Double-Tap or conventional single inflation. Patients requiring therapeutic post-dilatation for moderate or greater leakage around the implanted valve will not undergo randomization.

The main question is whether Double-Tap improves valve expansion immediately after TAVI, as measured using fluoroscopic X-ray images. The study will also compare blood flow through the valve, valve expansion and signs of valve thrombosis on cardiac computed tomography, procedure-related complications, and clinical outcomes. Participants will undergo echocardiography before discharge and at 3-6 and 12 months, and cardiac computed tomography at 3-6 months. Clinical follow-up will continue for at least 12 months, with annual follow-up thereafter until the last enrolled participant completes the 12-month visit.
primary_outcomes: Percentage valve expansion measured by fluoroscopy
title: Effect of Double-Tap Optimization on Valve Expansion and Hemodynamics in Balloon-expandable Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation: A Randomized Clinical Trial (DO-OPT TAVI Trial)

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether heat application combined with a shoulder support pillow reduces shoulder pain in adults (18 years and older) who undergo elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy and develop shoulder pain within the first 2 hours after surgery. The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does heat application with a shoulder support pillow reduce postoperative shoulder pain scores during the first 24 hours after surgery? Does it reduce incision pain and the amount of analgesics used within 24 hours after surgery?

Researchers will compare patients receiving heat application and a shoulder support pillow with patients receiving routine postoperative care only, to see if the intervention lowers shoulder pain, incision pain and analgesic consumption.

Participants will be randomly assigned to the intervention group or the control group.

Participants in the intervention group will:

Receive heat application with a towel-wrapped thermal gel pack (maximum 40°C) to the right trapezius and upper scapular region for 20 minutes at postoperative hours 2, 4, 6 and 8 Use a fiber-filled shoulder support pillow under the right shoulder and arm for 24 hours after surgery, except during mobilization

Participants in the control group will:

Receive no study intervention and will receive routine postoperative care only

All participants in both groups will:

Rate their shoulder pain and incision pain on a 0-10 Numerical Rating Scale at postoperative hours 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 20 and 24 Have their analgesic use during the first 24 hours after surgery recorded
interventions: heat application and shoulder support pillow
primary_outcomes: Shoulder and incision pain at 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 20, and 24 hours postoperatively.
title: Heat Application and Shoulder Pillow for Post-Laparoscopic Shoulder Pain

brief_summary:
Healthcare settings in low and middle income countries, clinicians are frequently required to manage a wide range of acute conditions under the constraints of time pressure, limited diagnostic resources, and variable availability of up-to-date clinical guidelines. Large language models (LLMs), which can synthesize and generate medical information in a natural language, have been proposed as potential clinical decision support tools. Most evaluations of LLMs in medicine have relied on standardized benchmark examinations or hypothetical case vignettes, often derived from high-income country contexts. MOOVE (Massive online open validation and evaluation) framework was developed to address the need for rigorous and context-sensitive evaluation of LLMs through a staged approach.

Study is a non-interventional, prospective study designed to test LLMs safely in real clinical settings, evaluate their performance against human care, and explore how feasible their future implementation in healthcare might be.
title: Massive Online Open Validation and Evaluation of Large Language Models for Resource Constrained Settings - a Study of Contextual Awareness, Safety, and Accuracy

brief_summary: Volleyball is a team sport that demands high levels of skill and strategy; it has gained significant popularity in Türkiye, particularly among adolescents. The spike-a key technical element of the game-is an explosive maneuver used to score points. Performance in the spike is determined by factors such as explosive power, vertical jump capacity, and technical-kinematic variables, with core stability and scapular stabilization playing particularly critical roles. Insufficient stability not only reduces hitting velocity but also increases the risk of injury to the shoulder and spinal complex due to repetitive overhead movements. In this context, Proprioceptive Neuromuscular Facilitation (PNF)-a comprehensive therapeutic approach aimed at enhancing muscular strength and neuromuscular coordination-is considered a potential intervention method. A review of the existing literature reveals a lack of research examining the simultaneous effects of PNF exercises (targeting the upper extremities and the core) on both upper-extremity and core stability in adolescent volleyball players, as well as how these effects translate to spike hitting velocity. By addressing critical components of volleyball performance and associated injury risks, this article aims to investigate the impact of PNF exercises on scapular and core stability, as well as spike hitting velocity, in adolescent athletes.
title: PNF Effects on Volleyball Performance

brief_summary:
This study will evaluate the safety and feasibility of administering umbilical cord-derived mesenchymal stromal cells (UC-MSCs) following mechanical thrombectomy in adults with acute ischemic stroke. Acute ischemic stroke occurs when a blood clot blocks blood flow to part of the brain, potentially causing brain tissue damage and neurological impairment.

The study will include 10 adults aged 18 to 70 years. All participants will receive standard stroke care, including mechanical thrombectomy to remove the blood clot. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups.

One group will receive standard care plus a single dose of 20 million UC-MSCs derived from donated umbilical cord tissue. The cells will be delivered through a microcatheter into the artery supplying the affected part of the brain. The other group will receive standard care without the cell treatment. Both groups will receive physical rehabilitation.

Researchers will follow participants for six months. They will monitor health problems and assess recovery, disability, blood markers, and brain scans. The main goal is to determine whether this treatment can be administered safely and feasibly. It is not yet known whether the treatment will improve recovery after stroke.
interventions: Allogeneic Umbilical Cord-Derived Mesenchymal Stromal Cells (UC-MSCs)
Standard Stroke Care Including Mechanical Thrombectomy
title: ARTEMIS: UC-MSCs After Mechanical Thrombectomy for Acute Ischemic Stroke

brief_summary:
Oral rehabilitation with dental implants in patients with severely atrophic maxillae often presents significant surgical challenges. Guided implant placement has been introduced to improve the accuracy of three-dimensional implant positioning and reduce the risk of complications associated with complex anatomical structures.

This prospective split-mouth clinical study aimed to compare the accuracy of zygomatic implant placement using two different materials for patient-specific stackable surgical guides: resin and metal.

Fifteen patients requiring bilateral zygomatic implant placement were included in the study. Each patient received a metallic surgical guide on one side and a resin surgical guide on the contralateral side.

Patient-specific surgical guides were designed using preoperative computed tomography (CT) data and three-dimensional virtual implant planning. Postoperative CT images were registered with the preoperative plans to evaluate deviations between the planned and actual implant positions.

Implant placement accuracy was assessed by measuring coronal, apical, and angular deviations. The study aimed to evaluate the influence of surgical guide material on the accuracy of guided zygomatic implant placement.
primary_outcomes: coronal deviation of zygomatic implant placement measured using CT ( mm)
apical deviation of zygomatic implant placement measured using CT ( mm)
angular deviation of zygomatic implant placement measured using CT ( degrees)
title: Comparing Resin and Metallic Surgical Guides for Zygomatic Implants in Patients With Severe Upper Jaw Bone Loss

brief_summary: This study investigated the effects of a 5-week Reformer Pilates exercise program on sleep quality, depression, anxiety, stress, and body mass index in 26 sedentary women. Participants completed 10 exercise sessions, with two sessions per week. Sleep quality and mental health were assessed before and after the intervention using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index and Depression Anxiety Stress Scales-21. Following the program, significant improvements were observed in sleep quality, depression, stress, and body mass index. These findings suggest that Reformer Pilates may be a beneficial exercise approach for improving selected physical and psychological outcomes in sedentary women.
title: Effects of Reformer Pilates Training

brief_summary:
The goal of this randomized controlled trial is to learn whether an education program based on the Turkish Nurses' Earthquake Management Model improves earthquake preparedness and earthquake intervention competence among nurses working in public hospitals in Türkiye. The model was developed from the experiences of nurses who worked during the 2023 Kahramanmaraş earthquakes and covers the pre-earthquake, during-earthquake and post-earthquake phases.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does model-based education increase nurses' earthquake preparedness? Does model-based education increase nurses' earthquake intervention competence? Are these gains maintained three months after the education?

Researchers will compare an intervention group, which receives the model-based education, with a control group, which receives no education.

Participants in the intervention group will complete a 13-session online video-based education program (about 15-20 minutes per session) through a university learning management system within 30 days. All participants will complete the Earthquake Preparedness Scale for Nurses and the Earthquake Intervention Competence Scale before the education, after the education and at a three-month follow-up.
interventions: Education Based on the Turkish Nurses' Earthquake Management Model
title: Testing the Effectiveness of the Turkish Nurses' Earthquake Management Model

brief_summary:
The goal of this prospective observational study is to learn whether diaphragm ultrasound and quantitative neuromuscular monitoring can predict early respiratory events after extubation in adults having elective surgery under general anesthesia.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Are lower diaphragm thickening fraction and diaphragm excursion before extubation associated with early respiratory events after extubation?
* How well do diaphragm ultrasound parameters and the train-of-four (TOF) ratio predict these events?

Participants will receive their usual anesthesia care. Diaphragm ultrasound will be performed at four time points: before induction of anesthesia, 5 minutes after induction, before extubation, and 30 minutes after extubation in the post-anesthesia care unit (PACU). The TOF ratio will be recorded with routine quantitative neuromuscular monitoring. Respiratory events will be recorded from extubation until discharge from the PACU.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of early postoperative respiratory events
title: Diaphragm Ultrasound and Neuromuscular Monitoring for Predicting Early Respiratory Events After Extubation

brief_summary:
Introduction and objectives

Saline irrigation and instrumentation during Retrograde Intrarenal Surgery (RIRS) causes elevation of intrarenal pressure (IRP) inducing intrarenal backflow (IRB). In an experimental study from 2025 Hinojosa-Gonzalez et al. demonstrated an association between elevated IRP and increased risk of bacteremia. The potential of elevated IRP and IRB to breach physiological barriers and facilitate systemic translocation of renal pelvic contents warrants investigation into their effects on parenchymal integrity and function.

Using contrast-enhanced MRI in a porcine model, Lildal et al. (2023) demonstrated segmental IRB with sharply demarcated areas of contrast distribution, predominantly at the renal poles. The preferential involvement of renal poles resembles the distribution of renal scarring observed in reflux nephropathy, raising the hypothesis that repeated pressure-related exposure may contribute to localized parenchymal alterations.

However, whether repeated ureteroscopic procedures are associated with similar persistent regional changes in renal structure and function remains unclear.

We therefore initiated an exploratory clinical study assessing renal structure and function following multiple ureteroscopic procedures using multiparametric MRI, DMSA scintigraphy and ultrasound elastography.

Materials and methods

This exploratory cross-sectional case-control study aims to enroll 10 patients with repeated unilateral ureteroscopic procedures and 10 healthy controls. Eligible patients must have undergone ≥3 ipsilateral procedures (RIRS/URS/URSL) and ≤1 contralateral procedure. Major exclusions include solitary kidney, metabolic or structural renal disorders compromising MRI analysis, chronic UTI, previous multiple PCNL procedures, and MRI contraindications.

All participants undergo serum creatinine measurement and multiparametric renal MRI (1.5T Philips Ingenia), including T1 mapping, heavily T2-weighted 3D imaging, diffusion-weighted imaging, T2\* imaging, and renal arterial flow assessment. Renal scintigraphy is performed using ⁹⁹ᵐTc-DMSA, with planar imaging for quantification of split renal function and SPECT for evaluation of cortical scarring. Bilateral renal shear-wave elastography (Mindray Resona I9 ultrasound system) is conducted to quantify regional parenchymal stiffness in five predefined regions per kidney.

Planned analyses will compare regional imaging parameters between patients and controls and between ipsilateral and contralateral kidneys, accounting for within-subject correlation. Segmental imaging parameters will be compared between groups and kidneys using linear mixed-effects models accounting for repeated measurements within subjects.
primary_outcomes: Renal Parenchymal Structural and Functional Assessment by Multiparametric MRI
Regional Renal Parenchymal Stiffness Assessed by Ultrasound Elastography
Renal Cortical Scarring Assessed by 99mTc-DMSA SPECT
title: Renal Structural and Functional Alterations Following Repeated Ureteroscopic Procedures: An Exploratory Multimodal Imaging Study

brief_summary: This clinical trial tests the feasibility of an electronic health record (EHR) integrated remote patient monitoring intervention to reduce readmission for patients with bladder cancer undergoing cystectomy. Cystectomy is the preferred treatment for locally advanced bladder cancer and involves removal of the bladder, prostate or uterus and part of vagina, and pelvic lymph nodes along with reconstruction of the urinary tract using a segment of bowel. Hospital readmission rates following cystectomy exceed 25% and are among the highest of any surgery. A significant barrier to identifying complications early arises from our inability to monitor patients once they are discharged from the hospital. The EHR integrated remove patient monitoring intervention helps with monitoring of symptoms after a patient's discharge from a cystectomy procedure and provides a direct line of communication between patients and their care team when concerning symptoms arise. This may reduce readmission rate for patients with bladder cancer undergoing cystectomy.
lead_sponsor: University of Michigan Rogel Cancer Center
primary_outcomes: Trial randomization meeting goal of 50 patients (feasibility)
title: EHR Integrated Remote Patient Monitoring to Reduce Readmission for Patients With Bladder Cancer Undergoing Cystectomy

brief_summary:
The goal of this study is to examine the effects of hearing aids and early intervention on hearing, language, and neural development in children with hearing loss in one ear, known as unilateral hearing loss. Our main research questions are:

1. Do children with unilateral hearing loss with earlier access to hearing aids and early intervention have better speech understanding in noise than children with unilateral hearing loss with later or no access to intervention?
2. Do children with unilateral hearing loss with earlier access to intervention have more typical responses in the brain than children with late or no access to intervention?
3. Do children with unilateral hearing loss with earlier access to intervention have better speech and language skills than children with late or no access to intervention?

Researchers will collect hearing, language, and neural data and information about each child's access to intervention to examine the longitudinal impact of auditory experience on these outcomes.

Participants and their caregivers will:

* Answer questions about the child's health, developmental, and hearing histories.
* Receive hearing tests and speech recognition tests.
* Complete tests of speech and language abilities.
* A subset of eligible participants will undergo magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and magneotencephalography (MEG).
title: Audiological Rehabilitation of Children With Unilateral Hearing Loss

brief_summary: This is a Phase I/II, multicenter, open-label, dose-escalation and dose-expansion study designed to evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics (PK), pharmacodynamics (PD) and efficacy of MBS314, a novel asymmetric trivalent trispecific humanized antibody targeting GPRC5D, BCMA and CD3, administered by subcutaneous (SC) injection in participants with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma. The investigational drug is MBS314 for Injection (high-concentration lyophilized formulation, 90 mg/vial, reconstituted to 90 mg/mL); this study is the first-in-human (FIH) study of this formulation. The study is divided into 2 parts: a dose escalation part (Phase I) and a dose expansion part (Phase II). In Phase I, eligible participants will be sequentially assigned to 1 of the 3 planned dose cohorts and receive MBS314 by SC injection using a step-up dosing (SUD) strategy, and dose escalation follows the Bayesian Optimal Interval (BOIN) design with a target toxicity rate of 33%. In Phase II, 1 to 3 dose groups will be selected based on Phase I results to further evaluate the efficacy of MBS314 at the recommended dose(s).

Phase I：Incidence of Dose Limiting Toxicities (DLTs)

Phase I：Recommended Phase Ⅱ Dose (RP2D) of MBS314
