brief_summary:
This study intends to adopt a prospective longitudinal research design to comprehensively evaluate patient-reported emotional stress and symptom burden in patients with advanced lung cancer and lung cancer brain metastasis during first-line and maintenance treatment, extract symptom clusters, and describe the longitudinal dynamic trajectories of symptoms and symptom clusters over time. Meanwhile, it analyzes the relationships between brain metastasis and emotional stress as well as symptom trajectories.

Patients will be divided into three cohorts according to the status of brain metastasis: non-metastasis, stable brain metastasis, and progressive brain metastasis. Differences in emotional stress, symptom burden and symptom cluster manifestations among subgroups will be further compared, together with their correlations with brain metastasis. This study aims to improve the understanding of the characteristics of symptom burden and symptom cluster profiles mediated by emotional stress in lung cancer patients throughout treatment.
primary_outcomes: To clarify the number of symptom clusters, changes in emotional stress, the composition of symptoms within each cluster, and their dynamic temporal trends during treatment
title: ePRO in Advanced Lung Cancer: Emotional Distress, Symptom Burden, Brain Metastasis

brief_summary:
This clinical study is investigating a new experimental medicine called LB-208, developed for the treatment of advanced solid tumors and lymphomas in adult patients whose disease has relapsed, not responded to treatment, or for whom no suitable standard treatment option remains. This is a Phase I trial, meaning it is an early-stage study in humans. At this stage, the main goal is not yet to prove definitive effectiveness, but rather to better understand the safety of the medicine, how it behaves in the body, and what dose may be most appropriate for future studies.

LB-208 is an oral compound that works by blocking a target called HTR1B. According to the protocol, it is considered a first-in-class treatment, meaning it belongs to a new therapeutic category and has a novel mechanism of action in this setting. The drug is given orally, once a day, under fasting conditions, in continuous 28-day cycles, with no breaks between cycles.

The study is open-label and uses a dose-escalation design. This means that both the medical team and the patients know which treatment is being given, and that the first groups of patients receive lower doses, which are gradually increased if tolerance is acceptable. The design used is the well-known 3+3 model: initially, 3 patients are treated at a given dose level. If no major safety concerns are seen, the dose is increased for the next group. If significant side effects appear, more patients may be enrolled at the same dose level or the escalation strategy may be adjusted. This approach helps identify the maximum tolerated dose and the recommended dose for future studies.

The main objective of the trial is to assess the safety and tolerability of LB-208 and determine the dose that can be recommended for further clinical development. To do this, researchers closely monitor adverse events, laboratory test results, physical examinations, vital signs, electrocardiograms, and other clinical parameters. A particularly important part of the study is the identification of dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs), which are significant side effects occurring during the first treatment cycle and help define whether a dose is tolerable.

In addition to safety, the study also examines pharmacokinetics, meaning how the medicine is absorbed, distributed, metabolized, and eliminated by the body. Blood samples are collected at different time points to measure how much LB-208 is present in the bloodstream and for how long. This information is essential to understand how the treatment works in practice and to help optimize dosing.

The study also includes pharmacodynamic and exploratory biomarker analyses. These assessments aim to better understand whether the medicine is having the expected biological effect and whether there are tumor or blood markers that may help identify patients more likely to benefit from treatment in future studies. Although this early trial is not primarily designed to prove anti-tumor efficacy, researchers will also evaluate preliminary signs of clinical activity, such as tumor shrinkage, disease stabilization, duration of response, and progression-free survival.

Patients taking part in the study must meet a series of eligibility criteria. In general, they must be adults with advanced cancer for which standard options are no longer effective or appropriate, have a good enough general condition to undergo experimental treatment, and meet the required organ function and laboratory parameters. As in all clinical trials, there are also exclusion criteria intended to protect patient safety, such as certain uncontrolled medical conditions, specific previous treatments, or other factors that could interfere with interpretation of the results.

Participation in this trial may offer some patients access to an innovative therapy that is not otherwise available. However, because it is a Phase I study, there are also important uncertainties. The benefits cannot be guaranteed, the most appropriate dose is still being defined, and unexpected side effects may occur. For this reason, patients are followed very closely by the clinical team throughout the study.

Overall, LB-208 / SERONCO-1 is an early clinical study designed to determine whether this new oral HTR1B inhibitor can be administered safely, to define the best dose for future development, and to generate the first clinical information on its potential role in treating advanced cancer. The knowledge gained from this study may help guide the next stages of development and determine whether LB-208 should move forward into later-phase trials.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Treatment related Adverse events (Safety and Tolerability)
title: Evaluation of LB-208 (HTR1B Antagonist) in Adult Patients With Relapsed or Refractory Solid Tumours and Lymphoma

brief_summary: High blood pressure (hypertension) is a leading cause of kidney damage, but detecting early kidney changes remains challenging with currently available tools. This study investigates whether kidney stiffness, measured by a non-invasive ultrasound technique called shear wave elastography (SWE), differs across different subtypes of hypertension and healthy volunteers, and whether it may serve as an early marker of hypertension-related kidney damage. Adults with essential hypertension, renovascular hypertension, and primary aldosteronism, as well as healthy volunteers, undergo kidney ultrasound with SWE measurements combined with standard clinical, laboratory, and vascular assessments, with the aim of identifying the independent factors influencing kidney stiffness and evaluating its potential role as a simple, painless, and widely available imaging biomarker of kidney damage
primary_outcomes: Mean renal cortical stiffness measured by shear wave elastography (SWE), expressed in kilopascals (kPa)
title: Kidney Stiffness Measured by Ultrasound in Patients With High Blood Pressure and Healthy Volunteers

brief_summary:
As survival rates following breast cancer surgery continue to improve, long-term survivorship management has emerged as a crucial clinical priority. In particular, two major clinical challenges remain: (1) maintaining medication adherence to 5 to 10 years of adjuvant endocrine therapy (tamoxifen or aromatase inhibitors) by actively managing treatment-related adverse symptoms, and (2) early detection and prevention of chronic breast cancer-related lymphedema following axillary lymph node dissection (ALND). Conventional passive monitoring relying on routine outpatient visits every 3 to 6 months often fails to detect daily symptom worsening or subclinical fluid accumulation in a timely manner.

This single-center, prospective, open-label, parallel-group randomized clinical trial evaluates the efficacy of an Agentic AI-based digital healthcare application (Pinkmate; a non-medical mobile health app) and a home bioelectrical impedance analyzer (InBody BWA ON) across two independent cohorts under a single master protocol. This study is conducted at Seoul St. Mary's Hospital and supported by the National IT Industry Promotion Agency (NIPA; Grant No. PJT-25-050007). Dual enrollment is permitted for patients meeting eligibility criteria for both cohorts (total target enrollment: 264 participants).

1. Cohort 1: Medication Adherence and Active Symptom Management (N=200) Two hundred breast cancer patients initiating or receiving adjuvant endocrine therapy are randomized 1:1. The experimental arm receives weekly electronic patient-reported outcomes (ePRO), conversational AI chatbot-triggered symptom questionnaires, clinician dashboard alert flags, and proactive telephone calls from clinical staff within 48 hours of an alert. The control arm uses basic medication reminders/checklists and quarterly ePRO collection without proactive alerts. The primary endpoint is the Proportion of Days Covered (PDC) at 6 months.
2. Cohort 2: Early Lymphedema Monitoring and Management (N=64) Sixty-four breast cancer patients who underwent ALND (including newly operated patients and prior ALND patients without clinical lymphedema) are randomized 1:1. The experimental arm uses a loaned home InBody BWA ON device at least twice weekly linked to the Pinkmate app; persistent dashboard alerts (3 consecutive days) trigger proactive phone counseling and early clinic visit recommendations. The control arm undergoes routine outpatient surveillance using the in-clinic InBody 770 analyzer and tape measurements, along with educational self-care app content. In both arms, standardized rehabilitation therapy is initiated based on in-clinic InBody 770 and tape circumference measurements using identical criteria. The primary endpoints are the percentage change in affected upper limb volume and the change in affected-arm ECW/TBW ratio from baseline to 6 months post-enrollment.
interventions: Cohort1: Pinkmate Agentic AI-ePRO Active Management Platform
Cohort1: Pinkmate Basic Medication Reminders and Standard Outpatient Care
Cohort2: InBody BWA ON Home Bioimpedance Monitoring and Behavioral App
Cohort2: Routine In-Clinic InBody 770 Monitoring and Educational App
primary_outcomes: Cohort1: Proportion of Days Covered (PDC) for Adjuvant Endocrine Therapy
Cohort2: Percentage Change from Baseline in Affected Upper Limb Volume
Cohort2: Change from Baseline in Affected Upper Limb ECW/TBW Ratio
title: Agentic AI App and Home Bioimpedance Monitoring for Endocrine Therapy Adherence and Lymphedema in Breast Cancer Survivors

brief_summary:
This randomized controlled trial investigates the efficacy of a mindfulness-based rehabilitation program delivered in a non-traditional environment rich in art and beauty (the University Museum, UD'A) compared to a traditional university gym setting (CARES) for patients with fibromyalgia.

The main question the study aims to answer is whether conducting mindfulness sessions in a museum setting can better reduce muscle pain (primary objective) and improve body awareness and quality of life (secondary objectives) compared to a standard gym setting. Additionally, the study evaluates autonomic nervous system responses using non-invasive thermal infrared imaging.

Furthermore, this protocol incorporates an exploratory home-based maintenance component-utilizing an illustrated educational brochure and a preregistered video of previously learned exercises-during a four-week follow-up period (T1-T2) to assess adherence, feasibility, and the maintenance of therapeutic benefits
primary_outcomes: Change from Baseline in Pain Intensity on the Visual Analog Scale (VAS)
Change from Baseline in Fibromyalgia Impact Questionnaire (FIQ) Total Score
Adherence to Home-Based Exercise Maintenance Program

brief_summary:
A single bout of exercise can improve cognitive abilities like memory and attention. These functions help us navigate through everyday life. However, we do not fully understand how exercise improves cognitive abilities. We believe that exercise improves the brain by increasing the amount of BDNF in the blood. BDNF is very important for learning and memory. However, we still do not know if BDNF responds differently to exercise between females and males.

The purpose of this work is to characterize potential sex-differences in the circulating BDNF response to acute exercise. We will test the hypothesis that males will have greater serum and plasma BDNF responses compared to females following a maximal exercise test.
title: Sex Differences in BDNF Study

brief_summary:
This pilot study compared two treatments for depressed acne scars: subcision alone and subcision followed by injections containing exosomes derived from human fat-derived stem cells and powdered polydioxanone (PDO). Subcision is a procedure that releases bands of tissue beneath the skin that pull acne scars downward.

Twelve adults with acne scars on both sides of the face participated at one clinic in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. Each participant received subcision alone on the left side and subcision with the additional injections on the right side. Three treatment sessions were performed four weeks apart, with a final assessment at Week 12.

The study examined whether adding the injections improved acne scar severity and overall appearance compared with subcision alone. Skin quality, treatment discomfort, recovery time, and unwanted effects were also assessed. A dermatologist who did not know which treatment each side received evaluated standardized photographs. This small study was intended to provide preliminary information to help plan larger studies.
interventions: Human Adipose-Derived Stem Cell Exosomes and Powdered Polydioxanone
primary_outcomes: Change in Atrophic Acne Scar Severity Using the Goodman and Baron Qualitative Acne Scar Grading System
title: Pilot Study of Combination Treatment With Subcision, Human Adipose Tissue-Derived Exosomes and Powdered Polydioxanone for Atrophic Acne Scars

brief_summary: Clozapine is the most effective antipsychotic medication for treatment-resistant schizophrenia, but it carries a rare, potentially life-threatening risk of agranulocytosis (a severe drop in white blood cells), which is why patients undergo regular blood monitoring. Most cases occur in the first months of treatment, and it remains unclear how much risk persists after the first year. This retrospective study will use existing electronic health records from Sheba Medical Center (February 2007 to August 2026) to describe when agranulocytosis occurs among approximately 2,020 patients treated with clozapine over up to 19 years of follow-up. The study will estimate the cumulative incidence and incidence rates across follow-up periods, examine whether risk after the first 18 weeks remains stable over time, and assess age, sex and psychiatric diagnosis as predictors. Each case will be individually reviewed to distinguish clozapine-related events from neutropenia due to cancer or chemotherapy. No patients will be contacted and no treatment will be changed. The findings are intended to inform policy on long-term hematological monitoring of clozapine-treated patients.
title: Time Course of Clozapine-associated Agranulocytosis Over 19 Years

brief_summary:
This study examined whether intermittent fasting helps people lose weight and body fat, and whether it affects muscle mass. The researchers compared intermittent fasting with a diet that reduced daily energy intake without limiting meal times.

The study included healthy adult volunteers aged over 18 years. Researchers randomly assigned 95 participants to one of three groups. The dietary intervention lasted three weeks, and 75 participants completed it.

Participants followed one of these eating plans:

Intermittent fasting with reduced energy intake: Participants ate 25% less energy than their estimated daily needs. They ate all their meals within a six-hour period each day.

Reduced energy intake without intermittent fasting: Participants ate 25% less energy than their estimated daily needs. They could eat throughout the day without a fixed eating window.

Intermittent fasting without reduced energy intake: Participants ate enough energy to meet their estimated daily needs. They ate all their meals within a six-hour period each day.

Researchers measured body weight and body composition before and after the intervention. They used a body composition analyzer to estimate body fat, muscle mass, and other body tissues. They also contacted participants weekly to monitor their progress and any problems related to the diet.

After three weeks, participants in the first group lost an average of 2.3 kilograms of body weight. Those in the second group lost 2.2 kilograms. The difference between these groups was not statistically significant. Participants in the third group lost an average of 1.1 kilograms, which was significantly less than in the other two groups.

All three groups lost some body fat. However, the differences in body fat loss between the groups were not statistically significant. The group combining intermittent fasting with reduced energy intake showed a greater loss of fat-free mass than the group practicing intermittent fasting without reducing energy intake.

The results suggest that reducing daily energy intake was more important for short-term weight loss than limiting meal times alone. Longer studies are needed to determine the lasting effects of these eating patterns on body weight and body composition.

Background:

Hypertension (high blood pressure) is a major risk factor for heart disease and stroke, yet many people do not know they have it. In Malaysia, nearly half of all adults with elevated blood pressure are unaware of their condition. Standard clinic blood pressure checks can miss cases of high blood pressure or falsely flag temporary stress-related spikes. While 24-hour Ambulatory Blood Pressure Monitoring (ABPM) is the standard method for an accurate diagnosis, it is not practical for large-scale screening.

Purpose:

The purpose of this study is to evaluate whether a novel Huawei smartwatch, which uses photoplethysmography (PPG) technology to estimate blood pressure, can accurately identify individuals at high risk for hypertension in a real-world setting.

Participants: Approximately 500 adults will be enrolled over a 24-month study period.

Screening: All participants will use the Huawei smartwatch screening tool to monitor their blood pressure estimates.

Validation: A subgroup of approximately 50 participants identified as high-risk by the smartwatch will undergo 24-hour ABPM (the clinical gold standard) to confirm whether they have high blood pressure.

Goal:

Researchers aim to validate the accuracy of the smartwatch screening tool against 24-hour ABPM to determine if wearable technology can support early detection and timely treatment of undiagnosed hypertension in the community.

This study was designed to determine whether vitamin D supplementation improved symptoms in children with irritable bowel syndrome, a condition associated with repeated abdominal pain and changes in bowel habits. It was hypothesized that vitamin D supplementation would reduce symptom severity and increase blood vitamin D levels compared with placebo.

The study was a randomized, placebo-controlled trial at the Department of Pediatrics, Aziz Bhatti Shaheed Teaching Hospital, Gujrat, Pakistan. It included 60 children aged 6-14 years who met established diagnostic criteria for irritable bowel syndrome and had low blood vitamin D levels of 10-29 ng/mL. Children were randomly assigned to two groups of 30 participants each. One group received oral vitamin D3 drops containing 2,000 international units once daily for 12 weeks. The other group received matching placebo drops without vitamin D for the same period. Both groups received routine supportive care, including advice on hydration, regular meals, diet, and symptom management.

Follow-up visits were scheduled at 4, 8, and 12 weeks to assess symptoms, treatment adherence, and possible side effects. The main outcome was the change in symptom severity from the start of treatment to 12 weeks, measured using a standardized symptom score. The secondary outcome was the change in blood vitamin D levels over the same period. Changes in both outcomes were compared between the two groups.

brief_summary:
Hospital-at-Home (H@H) programs provide hospital-level acute care in the patient's home and may reduce healthcare utilization while improving patient experience. Although H@H models have been evaluated in several acute medical populations, evidence regarding their safety and efficacy in a broad population of patients with acute cardiovascular conditions remains limited.

HeaRt@Home is a prospective, randomized controlled trial designed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of H@H compared with standard in-hospital care in clinically stable cardiac patients admitted to Tel Aviv Sourasky Medical Center. The study will enroll 150 adults hospitalized for selected cardiovascular conditions, including acute myocardial infarction following uncomplicated percutaneous coronary intervention, pericarditis or myocarditis, pulmonary embolism, post transcatheter valvular intervention, acute or worsening heart failure, or following Pacemaker or Implantable Cardioverter-Defibrillator Implantation.

Eligible patients will be assessed within the first 12-24 hours following clinical intervention and randomized to either continued standard hospitalization or H@H care. Patients assigned to H@H will receive hospital-level care at home, including continuous remote monitoring of vital signs and cardiac rhythm, 24/7 access to the hospital monitoring center, at least one daily home visit by a nurse, and at least one daily virtual assessment by a cardiologist. Laboratory testing, imaging, oral and intravenous medications, oxygen therapy, and additional specialist consultations will be provided at home as clinically indicated. A predefined emergency pathway will enable rapid transfer back to the hospital when required.

The study will assess safety outcomes including all-cause mortality, hospital-acquired infections, hemodynamic deterioration, acute kidney injury, venous thromboembolism, medication errors, 30-day readmission, and 30-day mortality. Patient experience will be evaluated using the 15-item Picker Patient Experience Questionnaire. Secondary outcomes will include length of stay, healthcare resource utilization, mobility and physical activity, sleep, arrhythmias, need for escalation to hospital care, and psychological outcomes.

The study aims to determine whether a structured, technology-supported H@H model can provide safe and effective hospital-level care for appropriately selected cardiovascular patients while potentially improving patient experience and optimizing healthcare resource utilization.
primary_outcomes: Composite Primary Safety Outcomes number of Events
title: Heart@Home Safety and Efficacy of Hospital-at-Home Care Versus Standard Hospitalization in Cardiac Patients

brief_summary:
Post-stroke fatigue is an overwhelming tiredness or lack of energy that does not get better with rest. It affects around half of people who have had a stroke. It can hold back recovery, make it harder to take part in everyday and social activities or to return to work, and reduce quality of life. There are currently no proven treatments for it.

Remote ischaemic conditioning (RIC) is a simple treatment that people can do at home using a blood pressure cuff on the upper arm. The cuff is inflated for 5 minutes and then let down for 5 minutes, and this is repeated 4 times, taking about 40 minutes in all. RIC briefly and safely reduces blood flow to the arm before letting it return. Research suggests this may help the body's cells produce energy more efficiently, improve blood flow and reduce inflammation. In our earlier small study (RICFAST), RIC done 3 times a week for 6 weeks was safe and well tolerated, and there were early signs that it might reduce fatigue.

This study (RICFAST 2) will find out:

* whether people with post-stroke fatigue can safely and comfortably do RIC at home more often (5 times a week) or for longer (12 weeks)
* whether enough people can be recruited to a study like this
* whether doing RIC more often or for longer might reduce fatigue more, and for longer, than the usual schedule or a comparison treatment
* how RIC might work in the body

Who can take part?

Adults who had a stroke between 3 months and 3 years ago and who have had troublesome fatigue for at least 6 weeks. People are being identified through stroke services, GP practices and community organisations in Sheffield, Doncaster, Rotherham and Barnsley (South Yorkshire, England).

What does the study involve?

60 people will take part. Each person will be put into one of four groups by chance (randomisation), with 15 people in each group. The groups differ in the pressure the cuff is inflated to (called "Pressure 1" and "Pressure 2"), and in how often and for how long the treatment is done:

* Group A (comparison group): cuff inflated to Pressure 1, 3 times a week for 6 weeks
* Group B: cuff inflated to Pressure 2, 3 times a week for 6 weeks
* Group C: cuff inflated to Pressure 2, 5 times a week for 6 weeks
* Group D: cuff inflated to Pressure 2, 3 times a week for 12 weeks

All the treatments cause a feeling of pressure in the upper arm. So that the results are fair, participants will not be told which cuff pressure is expected to have an effect.

Everyone will continue with their usual care. Participants will be shown how to use the cuff at home, can do the treatment at any time of day, and will keep a simple treatment log and symptom diary. The research team will phone or video call each week to check how things are going. Each participant will also wear a wrist activity tracker (Fitbit) throughout the study to record their steps, activity and sleep.

Questionnaires and tests of fatigue, mood, independence in daily activities, quality of life and walking will be done at the start of the study and 6 weeks, 12 weeks and 24 weeks (about 6 months) after starting treatment. The first three assessments take place at Sheffield Teaching Hospitals, and the 24-week assessment can be done remotely. Travel expenses are paid.

Thirty participants from Groups A, B and C will be invited to have extra tests before treatment and after 6 weeks: an exercise test on a bike, a magnetic resonance (MRI) scan of the lower leg muscles to measure how much energy is stored in the muscle, and a blood test for markers of inflammation. Some participants will also be invited to an interview about their experience of doing the treatment at home.

What do investigators expect to find?

Investigators expect that people in all groups will be able to do the treatment at home, and that RIC done more often or for longer will lead to bigger and longer-lasting improvements in fatigue. The findings will be used to design a larger trial to test whether RIC is an effective treatment for post-stroke fatigue.
lead_sponsor: Sheffield Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
primary_outcomes: Adverse events and serious adverse events
title: Remote Ischaemic Conditioning for Fatigue After Stroke 2 (RICFAST 2)

brief_summary:
This study aims to find out whether small daily monetary rewards can help older adults living in the community to regularly complete digital cognitive training. Cognitive training is a promising way to maintain or improve memory and thinking skills in older adults, but many people find it hard to keep training every day. Small rewards, such as a few cents or one yuan per day, have been shown to encourage healthy behaviors in other areas. However, it is not clear whether such rewards are effective for cognitive training.

The investigators plan to enroll 110 adults aged 60 years or older who can use a smartphone. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of four groups: a control group that receives no money, and three groups that can earn up to 0.2, 0.5, or 1 yuan per day for completing daily cognitive training tasks. The training takes about 15-20 minutes per day and is done through a mobile app. The study lasts 12 weeks with training, followed by 4 weeks without rewards to see if participants continue training.

The main question is whether the groups that receive money complete more training days than the control group. The investigators will also examine whether higher rewards lead to better adherence, whether cognitive function improves, and whether the effects differ by income level. This study may provide a low-cost way to help older adults stay engaged in cognitive training and reduce the risk of cognitive decline.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

Is it feasible for participants to take the probiotic supplement daily for 24 weeks and complete all study visits?

Does probiotic supplementation change blood androgen levels after 24 weeks?

What side effects or medical problems, particularly gastrointestinal symptoms such as bloating, gas, or changes in bowel habits, occur during the study?

This is a single-center, open-label pilot study without a placebo or comparison group. Researchers will compare participants' measurements before and after probiotic supplementation to explore changes in hormone levels and other health indicators.

Take one capsule of the probiotic supplement daily for 24 weeks.

Visit the clinic at the beginning of the study, at 12 weeks, and at 24 weeks for health assessments and blood tests.

brief_summary:
Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the third leading cause of cancer-related death globally. Surgical resection is the mainstay of curative-intent treatment, but the 5-year postoperative recurrence rate can be as high as 70%. Tumor heterogeneity is a major driver of recurrence and continues to complicate individualized treatment decision-making. For example, extended resection may improve radicality but risks hepatic decompensation, whereas limited resection preserves liver function but may leave microscopic invasive foci. Therefore, accurate preoperative evaluation of tumor invasiveness is critical to achieving a delicate balance between radicality and safety, and to improving long-term survival.

Multiparametric MRI is the most comprehensive noninvasive modality for assessing HCC invasiveness. However, most existing models are primarily data-driven and lack histopathological or molecular validation of their underlying mechanisms. They also lack precise spatial localization, limiting their direct application to surgical planning. A bottleneck is the lack of precise imaging-pathology correspondence, resulting from mismatches between macroscopic imaging and microscopic histology in both spatial registration and sampling adequacy. This gap also makes it difficult to establish a coherent link between imaging phenotypes and postoperative recurrence risk.

Therefore, this prospective observational cohort study aims to construct a multidimensional Imaging, Molecular, Pathological, And Clinical Outcome (IMPACT) database in patients undergoing curative resection for single BCLC 0/A HCC. The study has three major objectives:

1. Cross-scale imaging-pathology-molecular correlations: to spatially correlate multiparametric MRI and photon-counting CT (PCCT) imaging features with pathologic and molecular features, as well as with prognosis, thereby elucidating the biological mechanisms underlying imaging markers and phenotypes.
2. Prospective validation of prognostic models: to validate the predictive performance of the MERP, SPAN, and related models for recurrence-free survival (RFS), overall survival (OS), and other endpoints;
3. Imaging-guided individualized surveillance: to explore the role of abbreviated MRI (AMRI)-based surveillance in the postoperative follow-up of patients at high risk of recurrence.

By integrating imaging phenotypes, pathological immune microenvironment, genomic alterations, and clinical outcomes into a four-dimensional radiogenomic framework, this database will support a shift towards the "imaging-as-virtual-biopsy" paradigm, inform individualized surgical planning, perioperative treatment, and postoperative surveillance.
title: Integration of Imaging, Molecular, Pathological, and Clinical Outcome Data in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if offering a Family Accommodation Reduction (FAR) intervention to family members before OCD patients start CBT can improve CBT outcomes. The current study will offer 6 sessions of Family Accommodation Reduction (FAR) or OCD psychoeducation for the family member before the person with OCD receives 12 sessions of group CBT (GCBT).

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Is the addition of FAR associated with superior outcomes at the end of standard GCBT and at 3 month follow up in comparison to our control group?
* Is reduction in Family Accommodation a mechanism by which FAR is impacting the outcomes of GCBT?

Researchers will compare CBT outcomes between people whose family member received the FAR intervention versus psychoeducation and see if any benefits last at a 3-month follow-up.

Participating Family Members will:

* receive 6 weeks of FAR or Psychoeducation
* answer online questionnaires at several time points throughout the study about OCD symptom severity, quality of life, and level of functioning for the person with OCD.

Participating Patients will:

* complete 12 weeks of CBT for OCD
* answer online questionnaires at several time points throughout the study about OCD symptom severity, quality of life, and level of functioning.
primary_outcomes: Change in OCD Symptom Severity from Baseline to 3-Months Post-Treatment (Patient Self-Report)
Change in Quality of Life from Baseline to 3-Months Post-Treatment (Patient Self-Report)
Change in Functional Impairment from Baseline to 3-Months Post-Treatment (Patient Self-Report)
title: Family Accommodation Reduction in Adult Obsessive Compulsive Disorder: A Randomized Controlled Trial

brief_summary:
This randomized controlled trial compared two methods of pain relief after inguinal hernia repair: an ultrasound-guided transversus abdominis plane (TAP) block and local anesthetic injection around the surgical wound. The study tested the hypothesis that average pain scores differed between the two methods.

The study was conducted in the Department of Anesthesia at King Edward Medical University/an affiliated hospital in Lahore. Eighty male patients aged 18-60 years who underwent planned inguinal hernia repair were included. Patients were randomly assigned by a lottery method to two groups of 40 patients each. One group received an ultrasound-guided TAP block, in which bupivacaine, a local anesthetic, was injected into a space between the abdominal muscle layers to numb the nerves supplying the surgical area. The other group received the same dose of bupivacaine injected into and around the wound margins. Both groups also received paracetamol and diclofenac for pain relief.

The main outcome was the average pain score four hours after treatment. Pain was assessed using a visual analogue scale ranging from 0 to 10, where 0 represented no pain and 10 represented the worst pain. Further pain assessments continued for up to 24 hours after surgery, and patients were monitored for complications related to either procedure.
primary_outcomes: Mean Pain Score at 4 Hours After Treatment
title: Comparison Of Ultrasound Guided Transversus Abdominis Plane Block Versus Wound Infiltration With Local Anesthetics for Post Operative Analgesia

brief_summary: Advice on how long to limit physical activity after pelvic floor surgery ranges from 2 to 12 weeks and rests mainly on local tradition rather than data. This prospective observational study follows women undergoing a retropubic midurethral sling (TVT) for stress urinary incontinence or a laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy for pelvic organ prolapse at a single centre in Poland. For 6 weeks after surgery, participants keep a weekly diary of ten everyday activities, pain, and the reasons for not resuming each activity, and they complete validated questionnaires up to 6 months. The study does not change any aspect of treatment. Its main aim is to estimate the time to return to the pre-operative level of physical activity in each cohort.

brief_summary:
The goal of this randomized controlled study is to evaluate whether a wearable device-based, Life's Essential 8 (LE8)-guided management strategy can improve cardiovascular health in patients with chronic coronary syndrome (CCS).

Approximately 400 participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to either a wearable device-based management group or a data-blinded control group. All participants will receive routine cardiology outpatient follow-up every 3 months for 12 months. Participants in the intervention group will be able to view selected smartwatch data and will receive health and medication reminders as well as individualized LE8 feedback. Participants in the control group will also wear the smartwatch for data collection, but the monitoring data, reminders, and LE8 feedback will not be made available to participants in the control group.

The main question is whether the wearable device-based management strategy results in a greater improvement in the overall LE8 cardiovascular health score from baseline to 12 months compared with routine outpatient management.
interventions: Wearable Device-Based Monitoring and LE8 Feedback
Routine Outpatient Care With Data-Blinded Wearable Monitoring
lead_sponsor: China National Center for Cardiovascular Diseases

title: Out-Patient Proactive Observation With Wearable-Assisted Tracking for Cardiovascular Health Management

brief_summary:
To date, sport training methodologies have focused primarily on male/men/boy (MMB) athletes, with much less emphasis on female/women/girl (FWG) athletes. Relatively little research has been conducted to identify how to enhance FWG performance in sport and there is a lack of understanding of how training delivery models should be modified to optimize performance for FWG athletes. Typical physical training focuses on strength and fitness to improve power and endurance, depending on the sport. Evidence highlights the importance of combining Mental Performance (MP) competencies with physical training to achieve peak performance. Programs that interweave psychological and rehabilitation principles (including sensorimotor (SM) training) have demonstrated efficacy in individuals with pain and dizziness disorders. In addition, high-performance athletes have self-reported performance improvements and achieved record-breaking outcomes in their sport performance with SM training. Furthermore, these domains are shaped by broader sport and societal structures that are barriers to FWG athletes' equitable participation in sport. An integrated approach across pillars/domains has not yet been applied, nor in FWG sport specifically. Therefore, this new area of inquiry for the newly created SUPERGirl team will challenge current paradigms of sport development and specifically focus on elite FWG athlete training and performance requirements. With the combined transdisciplinary expertise in the SUPERGirl team, an integrated FWG athlete development program that goes beyond historical physical training and addresses FWG-specific needs will be co-created with coaches and sport partners. This innovative transdisciplinary model, integrating physical, SM, MP, and mental health training, could redefine the long-term FWG athlete development pathways and enhance sport experiences and performance for FWG athletes.

This study will recruit a total of 250 female, women and girl ice hockey players and skeleton athletes ages 11-26 years old.
title: Integrating Sport-Specific Comprehensive Training to Upscale Performance in Women and Girls

brief_summary: People with systemic lupus erythematous (SLE) have an increased risk of premature atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, which is believed to be caused by arterial inflammation. The aim of this study is to investigate the effects an interferon-targeting drug (anifrolumab) used for the treatment of active SLE on arterial inflammation. Arterial inflammation will be measured at baseline and after 4 months of treatment using Positron Emission Tomography (PET)/ Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) with a radio-labelled tracer (68Ga-DOTATATE). Inflammation assessed by PET/MRI will also be compared with clinical disease activity, inflammatory blood markers and in patients with and without coronary artery disease on computed tomography coronary angiography (CTCA) and/or myocardial involvement on MRI.
primary_outcomes: Comparison of coronary artery 68Ga-DOTATATE maximum tissue-to-blood ratio (TBRmax) after 16 weeks of anifrolumab compared to baseline
title: Effect of Anifrolumab on Arterial Inflammation in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Study

brief_summary: Objective: To investigate the effect of oliceridine on remifentanil-induced postoperative hyperalgesia and to observe its effects on postoperative pain scores, quality of recovery, and adverse reactions.Methods: A total of 130 patients undergoing gynecological laparoscopic surgery under general anesthesia were enrolled and randomly assigned to either the oliceridine group (Group O) or the sufentanil group (Group S), with 65 patients in each group. Remifentanil was used for anesthesia maintenance in both groups. Before skin closure, patients received either 0.02 mg/kg oliceridine (Group O) or 0.1 μg/kg sufentanil (Group S) via intravenous injection. The primary outcome measure was the mechanical pain threshold around the incision at 6 h postoperatively. Secondary outcome measures included mechanical pain thresholds around the incision and on the non-dominant forearm at 30 min, 6 h, 24 h, and 48 h postoperatively; Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) pain scores; number of effective patient-controlled analgesia (PCA) compressions; incidence of rescue analgesia; 24 h postoperative Quality of Recovery-15 (QoR-15) score; extubation time; post-anesthesia care unit (PACU) stay duration; and incidence of adverse reactions within 48 h postoperatively.
primary_outcomes: Mechanical pain threshold around the incision at 6 hours post-surgery
title: Oliceridine for Remifentanil-Induced Postoperative Hyperalgesia

brief_summary: Non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI), defined as deliberate self-inflicted destruction of body tissue without intent to die, is particularly prevalent during mid-adolescence, with prevalence estimated around 16-22% in community samples. Although distinct from suicidality, NSSI is a strong predictor of suicidal attempts. Yet intervention studies addressing self-injury urges and behaviors in youth remain scarce. The Cutting Down Program (CDP) is currently one of the most promising interventions for adolescents who self-harm. This three-month intervention, evidenced in a randomized controlled trial, integrates techniques from cognitive-behavioral (CBT) and dialectic-behavioral (DBT) therapies. Recently, an updated CDP protocol was developed to more directly address suicidality and involve parents in the treatment. This study will test the updated protocol with a sample of adolescents who self-harm, recruited from schools and treated by educational psychologists of the Israeli Psychological and Counseling Services (SHEFI). We will examine the intervention's effects on mental health outcomes (e.g., self-injury) and on potential mediators (emotion regulation and parental emotion socialization), to clarify its mechanisms of change.
conditions: Self Injurious Behavior Without Suicidal Intent
interventions: Cutting Down Program - a three-month cognitive-behavioral psychotherapy focused on reducing self-injury urges and behaviors in adolescents
title: Examining the Effectiveness of a Brief Therapeutic Intervention for Reducing Self-Harm Among Adolescents

brief_summary: Myocardial injury and infarction are common after cardiac surgery and are associated with worse perioperative outcomes. Hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF) is an important metabolic regulator that protects the myocardium. Roxadustat is an oral hypoxia-inducible factor prolyl hydroxylase inhibitor (HIF-PHI) approved for the treatment of anemia of chronic kidney disease; it enhances the hypoxia-protective pathway and erythropoiesis. We hypothesize that, in patients undergoing off-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), preoperative treatment with roxadustat may reduce postoperative myocardial injury or infarction. This pilot study is designed to test the feasibility of conducting a large randomized trial and to provide preliminary data on the potential effect of roxadustat on the occurrence of myocardial injury or infarction in patients undergoing off-pump CABG.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of participants completing the trial intervention
title: Roxadustat and Myocardial Injury After Off-Pump Coronary Artery Bypass Surgery

brief_summary:
Background:

Ambulatory Blood Pressure Monitoring (ABPM) is the gold standard for diagnosing high blood pressure (hypertension) because it tracks blood pressure continuously across day and night. However, standard ABPM requires a cuff that inflates every 15 to 30 minutes during the day and every 30 to 60 minutes at night. These frequent inflations often cause discomfort, interrupt sleep, and cause patients to abandon testing.

Purpose:

This study aims to evaluate whether a new cuff-based Huawei smartwatch can provide a less-disturbing ABPM experience. Researchers will test whether a reduced-frequency measurement schedule (e.g., 7 readings: 4 awake, 3 asleep) can provide the same diagnostic accuracy as a conventional, full 24-hour ABPM protocol (typically 48 readings) while improving patient comfort.

Study Design \& Procedures:

Study Population:

Approximately 500 adult participants will be recruited over a 24-month study period, with a targeted subgroup of 50 participants selected for clinical validation. The subgroup will represent normotensive, pre-hypertensive, and hypertensive individuals across diverse age groups and ethnicities.

Monitoring \& Comparison: Participants in the validation group will undergo standard 24-hour ABPM at an accredited clinical facility alongside monitoring with the Huawei smartwatch. Data from the smartwatch will be used to compare a reduced-frequency reading schedule against full 24-hour ABPM recordings.

User Feedback: Participants will complete questionnaires assessing comfort, sleep quality, ease of use, and overall preference between the smartwatch and standard ABPM cuffs.

Goal:

The main goal is to determine if a reduced-frequency wearable monitoring protocol can maintain clinical diagnostic accuracy for blood pressure and sleep-dipping patterns while significantly reducing patient burden and sleep disruption.
primary_outcomes: Mean Difference in Blood Pressure Measured by Reduced-Frequency Smartwatch Schedule Versus Standard 24-Hour Ambulatory Blood Pressure Monitor (ABPM)
Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of Blood Pressure Readings Between Reduced-Frequency Smartwatch Schedule and Standard 24-Hour ABPM
Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of Blood Pressure Readings Between Reduced-Frequency Smartwatch Schedule and Standard 24-Hour ABPM
Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC) of Blood Pressure Measurements Between Reduced-Frequency Smartwatch Schedule and Standard 24-Hour ABPM
title: Real-World Validation of A Minimally Disruptive Ambulatory Blood Pressure Monitoring (ABPM) Huawei Smartwatch in Malaysia

brief_summary:
Knee osteoarthritis is a condition that causes pain, stiffness, and difficulty moving the knee. Some people continue to have symptoms despite receiving usual treatments, such as pain medications, exercise, and physical therapy.

One treatment option is viscosupplementation, which involves injecting a gel-like substance called hyaluronic acid into the knee joint. Different products are available, but it is not clear whether they provide similar benefits, have similar side effects, or differ in cost.

The goal of this study is to compare two hyaluronic acid products, Mesoheal and Synvisc, in adults with knee osteoarthritis. The researchers want to find out:

* How well each product reduces knee pain.
* How much each product improves knee movement and daily activities.
* What side effects may occur.
* How the costs of the two treatments compare with their benefits.

The study will include approximately 160 adults who need viscosupplementation as part of their usual medical care. Each person's doctor will choose the treatment based on their medical needs and routine clinical practice. The researchers will not assign treatments.

Participants will be followed for six months. During this time, researchers will assess changes in pain, knee function, and any side effects that may occur.

The results may help doctors and healthcare providers better understand the benefits, safety, and costs of these treatments in routine clinical care.
lead_sponsor: Coordinación de Investigación en Salud, Mexico
primary_outcomes: Proportion of Participants Achieving Treatment Response at 6 Months
title: Comparative Effectiveness and Safety of Two Hyaluronic Acid Products in Knee Osteoarthritis

brief_summary: Non-speciﬁc low back pain is deﬁned as low back pain not attributable to an identifiable, known speciﬁc pathology. Non-specific low back pain accounts for over 90% of patients presenting to primary care and these are the majority of the individuals with low back pain that present to physiotherapy. It is thought that in some cases the cause may be an over-stretch (sprain) of a ligament or muscle. In other cases, the cause may be a minor problem with a disc between two spinal bones (vertebrae), or a minor problem with a small facet joint between two vertebrae. There may be other minor problems in the structures and tissues of the lower back that result in pain. The terminology becomes "chronic" low back pain when the symptom duration exceeds three months (CLBP). A variety of different types of exercise have been explored to treat CLBP, including low-to-moderate intensity aerobic exercise, high intensity aerobic exercise, core stabilization and muscular strength exercises and flexibility program. However, the most effective form of exercise as a method of rehabilitation for NSCLBP is unknown reflecting its complexity and more research is required. Objective of this study will be to compare the effects of Feldenkrais method with and without Dynamic Neuromuscular Stabilization exercises on pain, functional disability and quality of life in patients with non-specific chronic low back pain. Study design will be randomized clinical trial. Evaluation will be done by using NPRS, ODI and SF-12. Non-probability convenient sampling will be used and the subjects will be allocated to two groups by random allocation. Group A will receive Feldenkrais approach and Group B will receive Feldenkrais method with dynamic neuromuscular stabilization exercises. Both groups will receive hot pack for 15 minutes as basic treatment of non-specific low back pain before techniques application. Both groups will receive 12 sessions for the period of 4 weeks. Measurements of all the outcome variables will be taken at baseline, 2nd and 4th week. Results will be analyzed by using SPSS 24.
interventions: Integrated Feldenkrais Method with Dynamic Neuromuscular Stabilization exercises DNS
lead_sponsor: University of Management and Technology Lahore
primary_outcomes: Pain by Numeric Pain Rating Scale
Disability by Modified Oswestry Disability Index (MODI)
Quality of Life by 12-Item Short Form Health Survey (SF-12)
title: Integrated Feldenkrais Method With and Without DNS for Chronic Low Back Pain in Females

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate whether incorporating high-impact exercise (one-inch punch) into standard rehabilitation improves upper extremity function in adults following volar plating for distal radius fractures. The study will include 102 adult participants who have undergone surgical fixation for unilateral distal radius fractures and will follow them for 12 months post-operatively. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does incorporating one-inch punch training lead to better functional outcomes compared to standard rehabilitation alone?
* Does the addition of high-impact exercise enhance recovery metrics such as strength and mobility?

Researchers will compare two groups: one receiving standard rehabilitation plus the one-inch punch exercise, and the other receiving standard rehabilitation only. Participants will perform their assigned exercises over 6 weeks, with both groups undergoing similar physiotherapy and occupational therapy sessions. The experimental group will incorporate punching exercises targeting a cushioned pad starting from post-operative week 3, while the control group will follow the standard rehabilitation protocol without the high-impact exercise.
primary_outcomes: Health-related Quality of Life Measured by SF-12 Chinese (HK) Version
title: One Inch Punch High Impact Training Randomized Control Trial (1'' Punch HIT RCT)

brief_summary:
Radiculopathy is a neuromusculoskeletal disorder characterized by compression or irritation of a spinal nerve root, resulting in pain, reduced range of motion, sensory disturbances, muscle weakness, and functional disability. It commonly affects the cervical and lumbar regions and can significantly impair daily activities and quality of life. Various physiotherapy interventions have been used to manage radiculopathy, including exercise therapy, manual therapy, neural mobilization, and motor control training. However, the most effective intervention for improving pain, mobility, and functional outcomes remains unclear, highlighting the need for further research.

Kinetic Control (KC) Training focus on identifying and correcting faulty movement patterns through motor control retraining and postural correction, thereby reducing mechanical stress on the affected structures. Neural Mobilization (NM) aims to restore the normal mobility and physiological function of neural tissues, decrease neural mechanosensitivity, and improve nerve movement within surrounding tissues.

The objective of this study is to compare the effects of Kinetic Control techniques and Neural Mobilization on pain, range of motion, and disability among patients with radiculopathy. The study will be conducted as a randomized clinical trial. Participants will be recruited using non-probability convenience sampling and will be randomly allocated into two groups. Group A will receive Kinetic Control s, while Group B will receive Neural Mobilization. Both groups will receive conventional physiotherapy treatment, including hot pack, TENS application for 20 minutes before intervention.

The treatment protocol will consist of 12 sessions over a period of 4 weeks. Outcome measures will be assessed at baseline, the 2nd week, and the 4th week. Pain intensity will be measured using the Numeric pain rating scale (NPRS), range of motion will be assessed using Bubble Inclinometer, and disability will be evaluated using the Revised Oswestry Disability Index (RODI) for lumbar radiculopathy. Data will be analyzed using SPSS version 24. The findings of this study may provide evidence regarding the comparative effectiveness of Kinetic Control training and Neural Mobilization technique in improving clinical outcomes among patients with radiculopathy.
interventions: kinetic control training with conventional physical therapy
lead_sponsor: University of Management and Technology Lahore
primary_outcomes: Pain measured by Numeric Rating Scale (NPRS)
DISABILITY MEASURED WITH REVISED OSWESTERY DISABILITY INDEX (RODQ)
title: Comparative Effects of Kinetic Control Training and Neural Mobilization in Lumbar Radiculopathy

brief_summary:
Propofol is the most commonly used intravenous drug to start general anesthesia (induction). However, it often causes pain in the arm during injection, and remembering this pain after surgery can negatively affect the patient's experience and comfort. Adding lidocaine (a local anesthetic) to propofol reduces this pain but does not prevent it in every patient. Midazolam is a medicine commonly given to reduce anxiety, and it can also reduce the memory of events that occur after it is given (anterograde amnesia). It is not known whether midazolam reduces the memory of propofol injection pain after surgery.

In this study, adult volunteers aged 18 to 65 who are scheduled for elective surgery will be randomly assigned to one of three groups: (1) a low sedative dose of midazolam before propofol, (2) propofol mixed with lidocaine, or (3) propofol alone. Neither the participants nor the investigator giving the medication will know which group a participant is in. After surgery, once participants have recovered sufficiently, they will be asked whether they remember pain at the injection site during propofol injection. The study will also assess the severity of injection pain and the relationship between anxiety before surgery and injection pain.

All drugs used in this study are approved medicines given at doses used in routine anesthesia practice.
primary_outcomes: Postoperative recall of propofol injection pain
title: Effect of Midazolam Given at Induction on Recall of Propofol Injection Pain

brief_summary: This study will describe and evaluate the experiences and outcomes of women who have survived violence and also have medical needs. The intervention we are testing is a service called 'PATHH', a patient navigation service that extends after a stay in an emergency shelter. Some people who join the study will work with the PATHH patient navigator, and some will receive standard care at the community shelter. Participants who are assigned the PATHH navigator will receive additional support and help linking with services in the community during and after their emergency shelter stay. By doing this study, we hope to learn how patient navigation services affect the health and housing stability among women who have survived violence.
title: A Patient Navigation Trial for Housing and Health (PATHH)

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn how rare genetic muscle diseases change over time and whether muscle cells grown from a participant's blood can help researchers understand the disease. The study will include children and young adults under age 21 with a genetic muscle disease and a rare genetic change that may be suitable for a future personalized treatment.

The main questions are:

How do each participant's muscle strength, movement, and health change over time? Can muscle cells grown from a participant's blood show how their genetic change affects muscle? For some participants, can a potential treatment improve those cells in the laboratory?

Participants will be followed for approximately 2 years. Researchers will review their health, measure muscle function, and ask participants and caregivers about quality of life. Assessments may also include blood tests, muscle ultrasound, muscle MRI without sedation, optional nerve and muscle electrical measurements, and ankle-worn movement sensors for participants who walk.

Researchers will use a blood sample to grow muscle cells in the laboratory to better understand how a muscle condition develops and what potential treatments might work.
title: Personalized Disease Modeling for Rare Genetic Myopathies

brief_summary:
This trial enrolls patients with acute ischemic stroke. The key inclusion criteria are: patient age 18-80 years, within 72 hours of symptom onset, National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score of 4-24, motor dysfunction score of one upper and lower limb ≥ 4, and pre-stroke modified Rankin Scale (mRS) 0-2. Subjects will be randomized in a 1:1 ratio.

In addition to standard treatment, the intervention group (real stimulation group) will wear a non-invasive multi-channel electrode cap, typically using 16 channels, after MRI navigation and positioning. The device achieves focused stimulation of deep targets through current interference between multiple electrode pairs. This will be performed once daily for 30 minutes per session, with 10 days as one treatment course.

The control group (sham stimulation group) will use the same equipment and electrode cap. The stimulator will only apply weak current during the initial 30 seconds and the 30 seconds before the end to simulate the skin sensation of real stimulation, with no effective current output for the majority of the remaining time. This mode has been proven to effectively maintain the blinding of subjects and assessors.

Efficacy evaluation endpoints:

* Primary outcome: 90-day mRS score 0-2;
* Secondary outcomes: 90-day mRS score distribution; 90-day mRS 0-1 or recovery to pre-stroke disability status (if pre-stroke mRS \> 1); NIHSS score 10 days after treatment.
lead_sponsor: The First Affiliated Hospital of Bengbu Medical University
primary_outcomes: Proportion of subjects with modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0-2 at 90 days
title: Study on the Efficacy and Safety of Non-Invasive Brain-Computer Interface With MRI-Guided Multi-Channel Time-Domain Interference Stimulation in Treating Motor Dysfunction in Acute Cerebral Infarction Patients

brief_summary:
Fibromyalgia is a long-term condition that causes widespread pain, fatigue, sleep difficulties, and limitations in daily activities. Exercise and education about pain may help people manage these symptoms, but more information is needed about programs delivered in community settings.

The purpose of this study was to evaluate changes in physical function, pain, quality of life, and other health-related outcomes following a 12-week group program combining multicomponent exercise and pain neuroscience education in adults with fibromyalgia.

Participants attended one weekly session that included education about persistent pain and supervised exercises designed to improve strength, endurance, balance, and mobility. Assessments were planned before the program, at week 6, and at week 12. Attendance and responses to exercise were also monitored.

The researchers expected improvements in physical function, pain-related symptoms, and quality of life. The study involved one group of participants without a comparison group, so it was designed to explore changes during the program rather than establish whether the intervention caused those changes.
title: Multicomponent Exercise and Pain Neuroscience Education in Women With Fibromyalgia

brief_summary: Oral submucous fibrosis (OSF) is a chronic condition that causes stiffness of the oral tissues, reduced cheek flexibility, and difficulty opening the mouth. This randomized controlled clinical trial will compare the effects of intralesional autologous platelet-rich plasma (PRP) and triamcinolone acetate in patients with OSF. A total of 40 patients will be divided into two groups of 20. Group A will receive 1 ml of intralesional PRP, and Group B will receive 1 ml of intralesional triamcinolone acetate (40 mg/ml), once weekly for six weeks. Maximum interincisal distance and cheek flexibility will be measured before treatment, at six weeks, and at three months after treatment completion. The study will compare changes in these outcomes between the two groups to evaluate the effects of both treatments.
title: Autologous PRP Versus Triamcinolone Acetate in Patients With Oral Submucous Fibrosis

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to examine the effect of injection of adipose tissue derived stem cells in benign esophageal strictures in patients who have previously required at least 10 balloon dilations without satisfactory results on symptoms and esophageal diameter. This pilot trial will primarily examine the effects of the intervention on resolution of dysphagia and achieving a diameter ≥13 mm of the esophageal lumen. The trial will investigate dysphagia after two weeks, one, two and six months and diameter of the esophagus after one, two and six months. The trial will also record the following secondary outcomes: stricture diameter at each endoscopy, time to stricture requiring new dilation due to symptoms and diameter \< 13 mm as well as adverse events.

Participants will be required to undergo a procedure which starts by harvesting of adipose tissue from the abdominal subcutaneous fat. A concentrate of stem cells and supportive cells will be prepared on site, before balloon dilation of the esophageal stricture and then injection of the cell preparation within the dilated stricture.

Participants will then undergo follow-up after:

* Two weeks: telephone call, open question concerning side effects and dysphagia score
* One month: dysphagia score and upper endoscopy with measured diameter of stricture
* Two months: dysphagia score and upper endoscopy with measured diameter of stricture
* Six months: dysphagia score and upper endoscopy with measured diameter of stricture.

The patient will at any timepoint contact the hospital if symptoms occur and an endoscopy with dilation is needed (rescue dilation). The time from intervention to rescue dilation will then be recorded.
interventions: Adipose-derived stem cells and stromal vascular fraction
primary_outcomes: Resolution of dysphagia and esophageal stricture
title: Adipose-derived Stem Cells in Treatment of Esophageal Strictures

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether a silver-containing foam dressing (Mepilex Border Post-Op Ag) works as well as the standard dressing in preventing surgical site infection after cesarean delivery. The main questions it aims to answer are:

Is the rate of surgical site infection with Mepilex Border Post-Op Ag no worse than with the standard dressing?

How do the two dressings compare for other wound problems, wound-related hospital or clinic visits, and patient satisfaction?

Researchers will compare participants who receive Mepilex Border Post-Op Ag with participants who receive the standard dressing.

Participants will:

1. Have their cesarean delivery as planned by their care team
2. Be randomly assigned to one of the two dressings, which is placed over the incision at the end of surgery
3. Complete a short questionnaire about their dressing
4. Receive a follow-up phone call about 30 to 40 days after delivery (POD 30-40) to check on their wound
primary_outcomes: Number of participants with surgical site infection (SSI) within 30 days of cesarean delivery
title: The Mepilex Cesarean Delivery Trial / MEPIDEL

brief_summary: This single-centre, randomized split-mouth trial assessed clinical periodontal changes and acute systemic inflammatory responses when supra- and subgingival instrumentation was performed concurrently with oral hygiene instruction or after 90 days of oral hygiene reinforcement. Ten adults with periodontitis participated. One upper and one lower quadrant were randomly allocated to immediate instrumentation, while remaining quadrants received oral hygiene instruction and were instrumented at day 90. Clinical outcomes were evaluated at baseline, day 90 and day 180. High-sensitivity C-reactive protein was sampled before and 24 hours after each instrumentation session.
title: Timing of Oral Hygiene Improvement Relative to Subgingival Instrumentation

brief_summary:
This is a Phase Ib/II seamless, open-label, clinical trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of a serine/glycine-restricted diet combined with neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC).

The study consists of two phases. Phase Ib is a non-randomized, single-arm safety run-in phase enrolling 6 patients, all of whom will receive the experimental regimen (a serine/glycine-restricted diet plus CAPOX chemotherapy and long-course radiotherapy). The primary objective of Phase Ib is to assess the safety, tolerability, and dietary compliance.

If the safety criteria are met in Phase Ib (≥3 grade diet-related adverse event rate ≤20% and compliance rate ≥70%), the study will proceed to Phase II. Phase II is a randomized, open-label, parallel-controlled phase in which 120 additional patients will be randomized in a 1:1 ratio to either the experimental group (serine/glycine-restricted diet plus standard neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy) or the control group (standard neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy alone). The total enrollment is 126 patients (6 in Phase Ib + 120 in Phase II).

The primary endpoint is the complete response rate (pCR + cCR). Secondary endpoints include major pathological response (MPR) rate, R0 resection rate, mrTRG regression grade, event-free survival (EFS), progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), adverse event profile, changes in serum amino acid levels, quality of life (EORTC QLQ-C30), and nutritional status. Exploratory endpoints include gut microbiome diversity and tumor immune microenvironment changes.
primary_outcomes: Rate of Complete Response (Pathological and Clinical)
title: Phase Ib/II Trial of Serine/Glycine-Restricted Diet With Chemoradiotherapy for Rectal Cancer

brief_summary:
This study aims to evaluate and compare early radiographic healing of apical periodontitis following root canal treatment using bioceramic and calcium hydroxide intracanal medicaments.

Participants with apical periodontitis who meet the eligibility criteria will be assigned to one of two treatment groups. The first group will receive a bioceramic intracanal medicament (Bio-C Temp, Angelus), while the second group will receive calcium hydroxide (Ultracal, Ultradent). The assigned medicament will be placed inside the root canal for two weeks as part of the root canal treatment procedure.

Periapical dental radiographs will be obtained at baseline and at the three-month follow-up using the paralleling technique. Radiographic images will be evaluated to assess changes in periapical healing over time.

Periapical healing will be assessed using the Periapical Index (PAI) and quantitative image analysis with ImageJ software. The PAI will be used to evaluate the radiographic status of the periapical tissues. ImageJ will be used to measure the area and density of periapical lesions and their fractal dimension on periapical radiographs.

The findings from the baseline and three-month follow-up assessments will be compared to evaluate changes in periapical lesions and to compare early radiographic healing between the bioceramic and calcium hydroxide groups.

The study is expected to provide information on the effectiveness of bioceramic and calcium hydroxide intracanal medicaments in promoting early radiographic healing of apical periodontitis following root canal treatment.
primary_outcomes: Change in Periapical Index (PAI) Score From Baseline to 3-Month Follow-up
Change in Periapical Lesion Area From Baseline to 3-Month Follow-up
Change in Periapical Lesion Density From Baseline to 3-Month Follow-up
Change in Periapical Lesion Fractal Dimension From Baseline to 3-Month Follow-up
title: Early Healing of Apical Periodontitis After Root Canal Treatment With Bioceramic and Calcium Hydroxide Medicaments: Evaluation Using PAI and ImageJ
