brief_summary:
The research programme is an ambitious effort aiming to improve overall functioning and quality of life for young people with bodily distress. Bodily distress is a condition characterized by persistent physical symptoms (PPS), such as headache, nausea or abdominal pain, not explained by a well-defined disease. Over time, PPS can develop into a functional disorder, with detrimental impact on the young person's everyday life and opportunities. Thus, early intervention is crucial, but at present, access to specialized treatment of PPS to young people in primary care is very limited.

The investigators have developed the internet-based self-help programme My Symptoms Young as a new digital solution for early intervention of PPS. The intervention was developed using a high degree of user involvement (young people with PPS) and are now ready to be tested.

The goal of this clinical trial is to learn and preliminary test the possible effects of the internet-based self-help intervention program My Symptoms Young in young people aged 15-25 who experience PPS (physical symptoms presenting for \>3 months). The main question the investigators aim to answer is:

* What are the potential effects of My Symptoms Young In addition, the investigators aim to investigate if participation in the program can reduce overall symptom intensity and interference with daily activity in young people's lives. Finally, the investigators aim to examine if individual levels of health literacy (HL) and eHealth literacy (eHL) will modify the potential effects.
* The primary outcomes will be symptom intensity and symptom interference with daily activities
* The primary hypothesis will be: Symptom intensity and interference with daily activities will improve after the treatment with My Symptoms Young. The effect will be modified by levels of HL and aspects of eHL.

The investigators will include a total of 62 participants. The are no comparison group. Participants will be recruited from a health care professional in primary care (either general practitioner or practising pediatrician; from now on referred to as HCP). The HCP will determine whether referral to the My Symptoms Young programme is relevant. To guide this evaluation, the HCP will use pre-defined inclusion and exclusion criteria for participation. When a young person has been referred to the project group, a research assistent from the investigator group will contact the young person to provide more detailed information on the research project and the programme. If written consent is obtained, the young person will receive access to the programme. Throughout the intervention, the referring HCP is fully responsible for the health care of the young person. Referral and participation will be documented in the participants' primary care medical journal. If participants experience physical or psychological challenges during the project, they are advised to contact the referring HCP, i.e. the responsible healthcare provider.

The programme is accessed through a website, using either tablet, mobile or computer. It consists of seven modules, a closing module on relapse prevention, and a module targeting close relatives plus four tools: don't break the chain, goal setting staircase, symptom registration and notebook for reflections. The seven modules target symptom understanding, physical energy, resources and strains, thoughts, feelings, values, and self-care. Participants will gradually gain access to the modules. The programme encourages young persons to work with various exercises throughout the different modules but with freedom to choose what to work with. Besides text and exercises, the programme also includes explanatory animations, audio files on case stories, audio files on brief meditations and videos on physical exercises.

At first login (baseline), the participant will need to complete a set of questionnaires to access the programme. When completed the participant receives access to the programme. The researcher will follow up with participants by phone after one week if they have not logged into the programme and after three weeks if they have logged in but remained inactive. Participants can decide individually how long they wish to use the programme, but they are encouraged and recommended to engage actively at least twice a week for a minimum of 30 minutes. Participants will have access to the program for a total of 8 weeks. They will fill in questionnaires at three time points: Baseline (first login to the programme), End of Treatment (8 weeks after baseline) and 3 months after End of Treatment.
interventions: My Symptoms Young - an internet-based self-help programme for young people with persistent physical symptoms
title: My Symptoms Young - a New Internet-based Programme for Young People With Persistent Physical Symptoms in Primary Care: Exploration of Effect and Health Literacy Characteristics Among Users

brief_summary:
This study will examine how people feel after using the Musical Trail of the Ruisseau fleuri at the Montreal Botanical Garden and how they experience the mobile application. The researchers want to find out whether the experience is followed by immediate changes in emotions and feelings of connection with nature, and whether the application is easy and enjoyable to use.

The Musical Trail combines a walk through the garden with music created from electrical signals previously recorded from plants. These signals were converted into musical material and used to compose the music. Participants access the application on their own smartphones by scanning a QR code. As they explore the trail and identify or select plants, the music changes. Short texts also provide information about selected plants.

The main study will include 84 adults, with a target of 28 participants in each of three age groups: 18-34 years, 35-59 years, and 60 years or older. Participants must understand spoken and written French and be able to walk for approximately 20 minutes without sitting. An additional exploratory group of Montreal Botanical Garden employees is also planned.

Before their visit, participants will provide information about their background, their contact with nature, their concerns about environmental change, and feelings of distress related to changes in familiar environments. At the garden, they will receive instructions and use the application independently during an approximately 20-minute walk. A research team member will observe how they use it and remain available for technical assistance.

Immediately before and after the walk, participants will complete short questionnaires about how pleasant or unpleasant they feel, how calm or activated they feel, specific positive and negative emotions, and their sense of connection with nature. After the experience, they will also answer questions about the application, including its ease of use, musical and artistic content, difficulties encountered, and suggestions for improvement.

The researchers will compare questionnaire responses before and after the experience and explore differences between age groups. They will also examine whether participants' characteristics and existing environmental concerns are associated with their emotional responses. Observations and written feedback will help identify barriers to using the application and guide improvements to a future version.

All participants will receive the same Musical Trail experience. There is no control group. The study will therefore describe changes associated with the experience, without establishing whether the application itself caused those changes.
conditions: Emotional Responses, Nature Connectedness, and User Experience of a Music-Based Mobile Application in a Botanical Garden
interventions: Smartphone-Mediated Musical Trail in a Botanical Garden
lead_sponsor: Centre integre universitaire de sante et de services sociaux du Centre-Sud-de-l'Île-de-Montréal
primary_outcomes: Change in Affect Grid Valence Score
Change in Affect Grid Arousal Score
title: The Musical Trail of the Ruisseau Fleuri : Assessment of Emotional Responses

brief_summary:
Ovarian clear cell carcinoma is relatively more common in East Asian populations, and effective treatment options remain limited after recurrence. This study is designed to evaluate a novel combination treatment for patients with recurrent ovarian clear cell carcinoma.

This phase II, open-label, single-arm study evaluates the efficacy and safety of sacituzumab tirumotecan in combination with pembrolizumab in participants with recurrent ovarian clear cell carcinoma. Sacituzumab tirumotecan is an antibody-drug conjugate, and pembrolizumab is an immune checkpoint inhibitor targeting programmed death-1 (PD-1).

The primary objective is to evaluate the objective response rate assessed by central review according to Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) version 1.1. Secondary objectives include evaluation of progression-free survival, overall survival, duration of response, time to response, safety, and quality of life.
primary_outcomes: Objective Response Rate (ORR) assessed by the central review
title: A Phase II Investigator-initiated Trial of Sacituzumab Tirumotecan Plus Pembrolizumab in Patients With Recurrent ovarIan Clear Cell Carcinoma Previously Treated With Platinum-based Chemotherapy（NCCH2407/MK014）

The study starts with a dose escalation part (Part 1), followed by a dose expansion part (Part 2). A Drug-Drug Interaction (DDI) study (Part 3) may be conducted after the Recommended Dose of SIM0518 is determined.

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate the efficacy and safety of the polarized folded optical path reading and writing device in myopia prevention onset in 5-10 year old children with pre myopia. It will also integrate AI based fundus photography risk stratification, wearable environmental exposure monitoring, and far display screen behavioral recognition data to construct predictive models for myopia onset risk and intervention response, thereby establishing a precision prevention and control paradigm for this population. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* How can early risk identification, scenario based precision intervention, and objective efficacy prediction be achieved in pre myopic children?
* What is the mechanism of action of the device on the accommodation-choroid-axial length axis?
* What is the dose-response relationship among multispectral input, real world visual behaviors, and prophylactic efficacy?
* How does the multimodal collaborative regulatory mechanism integrating risk stratification, environmental monitoring, and behavioral recognition operate？ Researchers will compare participants using the polarized folded optical path reading and writing device against those not equipped with equivalent viewing distance extending optical devices (Intervention Group: using the polarized folded optical path reading and writing device; control group: not equipped with equivalent viewing distance extending optical devices) to determine the relative efficacy of the device in controlling myopia progression.

Participants will:

* If assigned to the intervention group, use the polarized folded optical path reading and writing device as their daily reading and writing tool for 12 months, with a target usage of ≥2 hours/day and ≥5 compliant days/week; if assigned to the control group, use myopia prevention desk lamps and posture correctors while maintaining their habitual visual behaviors.
* Attend clinic visits at baseline and at 3, 6, 9, and 12 months for comprehensive eye examinations.
* Maintain diaries documenting wearable environmental exposure data, real world far display screen usage behaviors, and any adverse events; additionally, undergo collection of color fundus photographs and AI derived fundus risk scores at the scheduled visits.
interventions: Polarized folded optical path reading and writing device
Eye-care desk lamp and desk posture corrector
title: The Efficacy of a Polarized Folded Optical Path-based Reading-writing Desk for Myopia Prevention and Control in Pre-myopic Children

brief_summary: Lumbar disc herniation is described by The North American Spine Society (NASS) as the confined movement of the disc material like nucleus pulposus and annulus fibrosis outside the limitations of the intervertebral disc space causing low back pain among adults. Low back pain become the most prevalent and common in adult generation. Lumbar disc herniation is the most common reason of low back pain in grown-ups of age saturation of 30 to 50 years. Lumbar disc herniation is affection almost 1 to 3% of the population per annum. There are many risk factors including alcohol, smoking, high intensity activities causing high load on your back or lifting high weight objects and genetic and environmental factors. The most affected and endorsed first line intervention protocol for lumbar disc herniation comprise of physical therapy management, life style adjustments and epidural steroid shots. This first line conservative management is used to avoid the risks of surgery and further complications. Spinal mobilization is used as the most effective and suggested option to help increase the mobility of the lumbar spine and reduce pain and disability chances in lumbar disc herniation patients. Clinical Pilates Exercise is used to upsurge core firmness and functional activity as well as boost the neuromuscular re-education in patients with disc herniation. The objective of this study is to compare the effects of spinal mobilization with or without Clinical Pilates on pain, lumbar mobility and disability in patients with lumbar disc herniation. Evaluation will be done by using NPRS, RODQ and Bubble Inclinometer. Non-probability convenient sampling will be used and the subjects will be allocated to two groups by random allocation. Group A will receive spinal mobilization and Group B will receive spinal mobilization along with Pilates. Both groups will receive hot pack and TENS for 10 minutes as baseline treatment of herniated disc back pain before techniques application. Both groups will receive 12 sessions for the period of 4 weeks. Measurements of all the outcome variables will be taken at baseline, 2nd and 4th week. Results will be analyzed by using SPSS 24.
lead_sponsor: University of Management and Technology Lahore
title: Effects of Spinal Mobilization With and Without Clinical Pilates in Patients With Lumbar Disc Herniationc Herniation

brief_summary:
This pilot study tests whether a mild form of brain stimulation to the cerebellum, combined with computer-based language therapy, helps people recover language after a stroke when a poor natural recovery is predicted.

People already taking part in a Johns Hopkins study of stroke and language recovery, whose early data suggest the aphasia is unlikely to resolve without treatment, are invited about 3 months after the stroke. Half begin 15 treatment sessions right away and half begin about 3 months later. Each session pairs 25 minutes of transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) over the right cerebellum with 45 to 60 minutes of language exercises, with a speech-language pathologist present.

The main question is whether language ability, measured with the Western Aphasia Battery-Revised Aphasia Quotient, improves more by 6 months after stroke in the group treated first than in the group still waiting. The study also checks how accurately a machine learning model, built from data collected in the first days after stroke, predicted each person's language ability 12 months after stroke.
interventions: Cathodal cerebellar transcranial direct current stimulation
primary_outcomes: Change in Western Aphasia Battery-Revised Aphasia Quotient (WAB-R AQ)
Mean Absolute Error Between Predicted and Observed 12-Month Western Aphasia Battery-Revised Aphasia Quotient
title: Cerebellar Brain Stimulation Plus Language Therapy for People at Risk of Poor Aphasia Recovery After Stroke

brief_summary:
This study compared two ways of doing strength training in healthy adults. The first, called Myo-Reps, is a time-saving method: one hard first set of 8-15 repetitions, followed by three short "mini-sets" of 3-5 repetitions with only 10-20 seconds of rest in between. The second is traditional training: three sets of 8-15 repetitions with 1-3 minutes of rest between sets.

Thirty-four adults were randomly assigned, by chance, to one of the two groups. For nine weeks everyone trained twice a week, under supervision, doing full-body workouts on 10 gym machines. The researchers measured how much stronger people became on each exercise, how much their fat-free mass (muscle and other lean tissue) changed, how hard the sessions felt, how much weight and how many repetitions were lifted, and how long the sessions took.

The aim was to find out whether the shorter Myo-Reps workouts can build strength and fat-free mass as well as traditional training.
lead_sponsor: Norwegian University of Science and Technology
primary_outcomes: Change in exercise-specific muscular strength (estimated one-repetition maximum, e1RM) across 10 machine exercises
title: Myo-Reps Versus Traditional Sets for Muscle Strength, Fat-Free Mass, and Time Efficiency

brief_summary:
The study is designed to establish a comprehensive myocardial energetic phenotype across a broad spectrum of cardiovascular diseases using phosphorus-31 magnetic resonance spectroscopy (31P-MRS).

And the study plans to enroll 1,000 participants, comprising healthy volunteers and patients with diverse cardiac conditions. Target cohorts primarily encompass heart failure syndromes and various cardiomyopathies, with a particular focus on non-ischemic and hypertrophic phenotypes, as well as ischemic and other structural etiologies.

By integrating 31-MRS with multiparametric standard CMR, this study aims to map disease-specific metabolic signatures. The primary outcome measure is the myocardial PCr/ATP ratio, serving as a direct in vivo marker of energetic impairment. Furthermore, the study aims to explore the coupling between metabolic phenotypes and structural remodeling (tissue characterization), mechanical dysfunction, and systemic clinical biomarkers. Crucially, the study will evaluate the prognostic value of these energetic phenotypes in predicting clinical outcomes, ultimately providing novel insights into the pathophysiology and risk stratification of cardiomyopathies and heart failure.
lead_sponsor: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences, Fuwai Hospital
title: 31P-MRS Myocardial Energetic Phenotyping and Prognosis Across the Cardiac Disease Spectrum

brief_summary: This study will test whether a combination of two medicines, zilovertamab vedotin (ZV) and lenalidomide, can help people with peripheral T-cell lymphoma that has come back after treatment or has not responded to previous treatment. The combination, called "ZiVLen", is designed to provide an alternative treatment approach that may use less chemotherapy than standard regimens. Researchers will evaluate how well this treatment works in controlling the lymphoma and will also assess its safety and side effects. The study will collect research biospecimens (archival tissue, and onstudy blood and stool samples) to investigate whether there are any immune system changes in participants who's lymphoma responds to the treatment compared to those who do not. In addition, health related quality of life surveys (patient reported outcome measures \[PROMS\]) will be collected to better understand whether the treatment and/or trial has impacted the health related quality of life of participants in their own voice. The results of this study will help determine whether ZiVLen should be studied further in larger clinical trials.
primary_outcomes: Rate of complete response to up to 6 cycles of combination zilovertamab vedotin and lenalidomide
title: Zilovertamab Vedotin and Lenalidomide (ZiVLen) Therapy for Relapsed/Refractory Peripheral T-Cell Lymphoma

brief_summary:
This study was designed to assess whether daily L-arginine supplementation could prevent preeclampsia in pregnant women at increased risk. Preeclampsia, a pregnancy complication involving high blood pressure and possible organ damage, was the condition of interest. The study hypothesis was that L-arginine supplementation would be more effective than placebo in preventing preeclampsia before delivery.

The study was designed as a randomized controlled trial at the Department of Gynaecology and Obstetrics, Bahawal Victoria Hospital, Bahawalpur, Pakistan. Eligible participants were women aged 18-40 years with a single-baby pregnancy at 20 weeks and an increased risk of preeclampsia based on their personal or family medical history. The protocol specified assignment by chance to either daily oral L-arginine supplementation or placebo until delivery.

Follow-up visits were scheduled every three weeks during pregnancy and two weeks after childbirth. Assessments included blood pressure, urine testing for protein, and monitoring for side effects. The main outcome was the proportion of women who remained free of preeclampsia until delivery. Other planned assessments included pregnancy complications, delivery outcomes, birth weight, newborn health, and admission to intensive care.
primary_outcomes: Percentage of Participants Who Remained Free of Preeclampsia Until Delivery
title: Efficacy Of Supplemental L-Arginine in Preventing Preeclampsia in Pregnant Women

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to find out whether virtual simulation helps nursing students learn how to manage postpartum hemorrhage (heavy bleeding after childbirth). Third-year nursing students taking the Obstetrics and Gynecology Nursing course were randomly assigned to one of three groups: virtual simulation, case study, or control. Students' knowledge was measured with a postpartum hemorrhage knowledge test, and their skills were assessed with a skill evaluation checklist during a hybrid simulation scenario. The results will show whether virtual simulation improves students' knowledge and skills compared with case study and standard education.
title: The Effect of Using Virtual Simulation on Students' Knowledge and Skill Levels Regarding Postpartum Hemorrhage Management

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial was to learn whether a single interactive mental health education session improves mental health literacy among senior high school students in a remote area on the Indonesia-Malaysia land border (Sambas Regency, West Kalimantan, Indonesia). The main question was whether students who attended the session would score higher on the Mental Health Knowledge Questionnaire immediately afterwards than students who received a printed leaflet, after accounting for their scores before the activity.

Researchers compared intact classes that attended the session with classes that received a printed mental health leaflet. Participants completed the questionnaire before the activity, then either attended one face-to-face session of about 60 minutes or received the leaflet, and completed the same questionnaire again immediately afterwards on the same day. This record was registered after data collection had been completed.
title: School-Based Mental Health Education on Mental Health Literacy Among Adolescents

brief_summary:
This multicenter, randomized clinical trial will assess whether intravenous tenecteplase given before interhospital transfer improves outcomes compared with direct transfer without tenecteplase. Eligible participants are adults with acute ischemic stroke caused by occlusion of the M1 segment or proximal dominant M2 segment of the middle cerebral artery, more than 4.5 hours and no more than 24 hours after symptom onset or the last known well time.

Participants will be assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive tenecteplase before transfer or to undergo direct transfer without study-related intravenous thrombolysis. At the receiving stroke center, both groups will be evaluated for endovascular therapy and treated when clinically indicated. The primary outcome is the proportion of participants with a modified Rankin Scale score of 0-2 at 90 days after randomization. The study will also assess neurological improvement, vessel reopening, intracranial hemorrhage, and other clinical outcomes.
